stories.title: Julius Randle rips Nets teammates for showing ‘no pride’ in embarrassing loss: ‘A lot of excuses’
stories.summary: Julius Randle slammed his Nets teammates for showing "no pride" after a 30-point loss to the Bulls dropped Brooklyn to a 3-11 record on the season.
stories.detailText: New York Post may be compensated and/or receive an affiliate commission if you click or buy through our links. Featured pricing is subject to change. Julius Randle of the Brooklyn Nets looks on during a game against the Chicago Bulls at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y., Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Julius Randle has been in the NBA for 13 seasons, including three All-Star appearances as a member of the Knicks. Well before he said in a post-game news conference Wednesday night that he was embarrassed about the Nets’ lack of effort in a blowout loss to the Bulls , his frustration and anger were already evident. As seen and heard in a since-viral video taken from behind the bench at the end of the third quarter, Randle admonished his teammates for several seconds for showing “no pride” in their latest defeat, which he later called “one of the worst games I’ve ever been a part of” in his career. Julius Randle of the Brooklyn Nets looks on during a game against the Chicago Bulls at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y., Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “Just a little frustrated. … It was tough,” Randle said after the Nets fell to 3-11 entering Friday’s home game against Orlando. “Like I said, I’ve been in the league for 13 years, and it just felt like five individuals out there. I was just trying to somehow, some way, relay to the group that winning is the most important thing, not individuals. “So we gotta find a way to get connected as a group and put that first. But I have to find a way to be better too, and I put that on me.” With seven first-round picks over the past two seasons, the Nets still are rebuilding, but Randle and former NBA champion Michael Porter Jr. are among the veterans on hand to help coach Jordi Fernández avoid such alarming performances. Wednesday’s loss — with Julius Erving and other former ABA champion teammates on hand — marked the third consecutive game in which the Nets got walloped in the first half. They coughed up at least 70 points through two quarters in those losses to Memphis, Philadelphia and Chicago — the first time that’s happened in their franchise history in the NBA. Norman Powell (24) of the Chicago Bulls drives to the basket against Julius Randle (30) of the Brooklyn Nets in New York on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Getty Images Randle had spoken after the loss to the 76ers about the importance of “punching first,” but the Bulls connected for a franchise record 15 3-pointers in the first half alone, and they shot 21-for-46 on 3s in their 30-point win. “They were living in our paint at will, getting into the paint and spraying the basketball. … I felt like we didn’t stop them at all from getting in the paint,” Randle said. “As a man, you gotta look yourself in the mirror and come into work and figure out what matters. CHECK OUT THE LATEST NBA STANDINGS AND NETS STATS “If winning is what matters, then you’ll do the necessary things to win. But I think it’s not there right now.” Fernández said he has appreciated the efforts of Randle and Porter, who both average more than 20 points per game for the season, although Porter managed just five on 1-for-7 shooting in 27 minutes against Chicago. “They’ve been amazing in practice. They work every day, and it’s not pulling teeth at all,” Fernández said. Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle (30) speaks with head coach Jordi Fernández during a game against the Chicago Bulls, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in Brooklyn. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “Now, I need to see it on the court. Obviously, as starters and veterans, they’re more responsible, but I’ve been very happy with them. I know they can be a big part of us doing things better. No excuses here. I think from the beginning both of those guys, when things don’t go well, they put it on themselves, as [I do] myself. That’s what you’re supposed to [do] as a leader.” The 31-year-old Randle added that he’s “always going to hold myself accountable and figure out ways or find ways to do more. I think [that’s true] when you find ways to win, but when you lose, you find excuses. It seems like a lot of excuses right now.” Fernández also used phrases such as “selfishness” and “not playing hard” and “guys pointing fingers” to describe Wednesday’s no-show. “Obviously, I’m the one in front right there, and I don’t want my team to play like this,” he said. The third-year head coach acknowledged that an immediate priority must be to fix the defensive effort, which also featured 18 second-chance points by the Bulls in the first quarter. “Obviously, we all feel embarrassed for the performance,” Fernández said, “but you gotta watch and learn and move on.” Joshua Jefferson, Drake Powell and Ben Saraf were recalled from Long Island of the G-League. Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jonathan Isaac (knee) will be out for Orlando.

stories.title: Karl-Anthony Towns is letting his Knicks play speak loudest in face of uncertainty
stories.summary: In his own words, this should be an uncomfortable situation for Karl-Anthony Towns.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS — In his own words, this should be an uncomfortable situation for Karl-Anthony Towns. Regardless, it’s produced some of the best basketball of his career . Before the season, when Towns still was publicly pushing for a contract extension from the Knicks, he said he wanted his long-term future settled “so I can feel as comfortable as possible.” Without a new deal, he said, “there’s no comfortability to be had.” Karl-Anthony Towns rises up for a rebound during the Knicks’ win over the Raptors on Nov. 17, 2026, in Toronto. NBAE via Getty Images That new deal, of course, never materialized, as the Knicks shut down all extension negotiations for the season while navigating owner James Dolan’s mandate to stay under the second apron. It left Towns in that uncomfortable situation. He’s responded by making a loud statement to Knicks brass with his play. “I got a job to do, at the end of the day,” Towns said before the team’s game against the Timberwolves on Thursday. “I gotta come here and put that jersey on and do what’s best for my brothers and the guys they have in my locker room. So, I’m just here to do my job.” Towns entered Thursday night’s game averaging 21.2 points, 3.9 assists and a league-high 14.1 rebounds while shooting 54.5 percent from the field and 40.0 percent from 3-point range. Karl-Anthony Towns looks to make a pass while being defended by Collin Murray-Boyles during the Knicks’ road win over the Raptors on Nov. 17, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images He has been by far the most consistently strong performer through the Knicks’ rocky first few weeks of their championship defense. He’s shown no signs of letting that discomfort affect him. If anything, it is fueling him. “I gotta put that jersey on and put the best performance out there for my teammates,” Towns said. “So, that’s all I really think about.” Towns’ standout performances came just as he returned to Minnesota , where he spent the first nine years of his career. He didn’t want to opine Thursday about whether winning a championship with the Knicks validates the move for New York and means it won the blockbuster trade with the Timberwolves, which sent Julius Randle and Donte DiVincenzo back to Minnesota. But at this point, it’s a clear Knicks win. Karl-Anthony Towns looks to make a move on Collin Murray-Boyles during the Knicks’ road win over the Raptors on Nov. 17, 2026. Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images But it doesn’t make being back any less emotional for Towns, who still has a painting of him and his mother and father hugging that the Timberwolves gifted him. They were the last team he played for before his mother passed away during the COVID-19 pandemic. “I still have so much love for this place,” Towns said. “It doesn’t go away. I think it’s actually grown as I’ve been away. I think that, even for me and my dad, we were just driving around the city and just going to places. We went to eat at a spot we love to go here. It always hits home. This is the last place that I got to play basketball with my mom. I got to see the kids be young before now. Jolani, my niece, who was in my rookie of the year photo actually in here, she was a baby, and now she’s in high school. It’s a different part of life, but it’s a part of life that I really enjoy.” Thursday was the third time Towns returned as an opponent. But it was the first time as a champion. “It’s always great to be home and to be back here,” Towns said. “Nine years of my life, some amazing years, amazing moments. Yeah, it’s special to be back. Obviously, it’s bittersweet to come back with a championship because I wanted to win it here so bad for the city, for Minneapolis, for Minnesota, for all the people who haven’t seen an NBA championship here. But it’s great to be able to come back and to be able to see friends, people I call family here.”

stories.title: Mavericks lean into Cooper Flagg's peanut butter and jelly trend with pop-up
stories.summary: The Dallas Mavericks' pop-up includes creamy peanut butter and grape jelly on white sourdough bread.
stories.detailText: Dallas Mavericks fans might not be able to hoop like Cooper Flagg , but they can eat like him. The Mavericks announced Thursday that they are bringing "The Jam Box" pop-up concession stand to American Airlines Center exclusively for Saturday's game against the LA Clippers , courtesy of Levy Restaurants. Fans will be able to indulge in the limited-edition offering of creamy peanut butter and grape jelly on white sourdough bread -- Flagg's preferred combination. They are set to be priced at $3.20, a nod to Flagg's No. 32, with just 320 sandwiches supplied and given out in a sandwich bag sealed with a sticker. They are available while supplies last on the American Airlines Center's main plaza level outside section 117. The forward has been spotted eating the combination on the bench during games and even in news conferences this season. He explained on Nov. 8 that the in-game snack is because he's trying to put on weight and gain muscle. "So those requirements I got to meet. I'm just trying to stay ahead of it," Flagg said . "We got another game [on Nov. 9]. So just trying to get my calories and stay ahead of it and be ready for another one." He clarified that he's a smooth peanut butter and grape jelly enthusiast, no different than what the Mavericks are giving away Saturday. Flagg added that he also enjoys a simple peanut butter and banana sandwich, while sometimes adding honey. The 19-year-old is currently averaging 24.2 points, 6.6 rebounds and 6.4 assists per game. As his PB&J trend gained traction, Flagg dropped 43 points, 10 rebounds and six assists in a 125-122 win against the Indiana Pacers on Nov. 9. He then forgot to bring his sandwich to the postgame news conference, before posting an image of it while in his car . NBA players and peanut butter and jelly sandwiches might be the epitome of the saying: "we go together like peanut butter and jelly." During his tenure with the Boston Celtics in the 2007-08 campaign, Kevin Garnett ate a sandwich before a game, proceeded to play well and started a tradition that other NBA players have adopted since then . Now, Mavs fans can potentially start their own.

stories.title: Warriors vs. Grizzlies injury report: Draymond Green out, Al Horford returns
stories.summary: The full slate of injuries for Thursday’s game between Golden State and Memphis.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - APRIL 17: Draymond Green #23 of the Golden State Warriors reacts during the second half of an NBA play-in tournament game at Mortgage Matchup Center on April 17, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Suns defeated the Warriors 111-96. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Golden State Warriors are closing out a brutal five-game road trip tonight, and hoping to salvage it with a win against the Memphis Grizzlies . If they were to win, it would be a little bit of payback for the second game of the season, when the Dubs blew a late double-digit lead against the Grizzlies. Both teams are missing some serious talent, but thankfully, Al Horford is returning for Golden State after not playing in Wednesday’s loss to the Dallas Mavericks . Here’s the full injury report. Warriors Out — Steph Curry (right oblique tear) With every passing game, it becomes more and more obvious that the Warriors need Curry back. Unfortunately, there’s still not a timeline for his return, though he’ll be re-evaluated next week. Out — Draymond Green (right elbow injury management) The Dubs are without their best offensive player in Curry and their best defensive player in Green. What could possibly go wrong? Out — Brandon Williams (left hamstring strain) Williams will be re-evaluated on Saturday, so there’s a chance that this is the last game he misses before returning. That would be nice, as the Dubs are really missing his offense off the bench. Out — Jimmy Butler III (right ACL repair surgery) Out — Moses Moody (left patellar tendon repair surgery) Out — Kristaps Porziņģis (not with team) Same news as always with this group. But we’re pushing through the season, which means Butler and Moody are getting closer to returning. Questionable — LJ Cryer (left low back soreness) Cryer has stepped into a large role — a starting role, even — with Curry and Williams injured. His three-point shooting is critical for the Warriors when Curry is out, so hopefully he’s able to play tonight despite the back issue. Grizzlies Out — Ty Jerome (right hip impingement) The former Warrior has been a revelation in his second season with the Grizzlies, after injuries cost him most of his first year with the team. Despite entering the season averaging just 9.3 points per game, Jerome has positively exploded for 25.4 points, while also dishing 5.3 assists. He scored 28 points when these teams met in October, but will miss his fourth straight game. Out — Zach Edey (left ankle injury management) The Warriors are getting a little bit of a gift with Edey’s absence, as they struggle to contain size. Edey is one of the largest players in the NBA, and had 10 rebounds and two blocks in the last game against the Warriors, despite only playing 22 minutes. Out — Scotty Pippen Jr. (lumbar disc herniation) Pippen’s been dealing with a back issue for a while now, as this will be his 11th consecutive absence. Hopefully he’s back on the court soon. Out — GG Jackson II (left 5th metatarsal fracture) Jackson was having a solid fourth season, but suffered an injury last week that will cost him a few months. He’s expected to be re-evaluated sometime around the All-Star break. Out — Richie Saunders (right knee surgery) Saunders, who was drafted 32nd overall in June, tore his ACL in February, so he’s likely still a ways away from making his NBA debut. Questionable — Isaiah Stewart (illness) Beef Stew has been solid in his first season in Memphis, averaging 10.9 points despite playing less than 20 minutes per night. He’s only grabbing 3.3 rebounds, but even so, his size could be an issue for the Dubs. Enjoy the game, everyone. It tips off at 5:00 p.m. PT on NBC Sports Bay Area.

stories.title: LSU president orders RJ Luis benched amid SEC expulsion threat
stories.summary: LSU reversed course and benched RJ Luis after his lawyer said the SEC threatened to expel the school if the guard continued playing.
stories.detailText: The RJ Luis Jr. drama came to an inevitable and ignominious end — or, at least, pause — Thursday, Nov. 19, as the LSU guard is to be benched by Will Wade at the behest of LSU President Wade Rousseau after playing in one game on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Luis, who played under the protection of a court order, scored 11 points for the Tigers in his season debut against Louisiana-Monroe, which ended in a 79-67 LSU win. Luis was added to the roster Tuesday, Nov. 17 , with Rousseau saying in a statement: "LSU is a member institution that will act in accordance with that order. The conference has confirmed it will do the same and has stated in writing that it 'will abide by the terms of the preliminary injunction while it remains in place and will not impose penalties or fines on LSU if (it) places Mr. Luis on its men's basketball roster." 'Really gross': Dan Hurley rips NCAA basketball eligibility crisis, blames coaches Toppmeyer: Greg Sankey once ruled college football. Now, he’s losing grip on SEC In a course reversal Thursday, Rousseau said: "In my role as President of the LSU System, after further review, I have instructed LSU Men's Basketball Coach Will Wade to not play RJ Luis." In a statement, Luis' lawyer Elliot Abrams said there were threats of expelling LSU from the SEC if Luis continued to play. “The SEC’s decision to threaten a member with expulsion if it plays an eligible student-athlete is reprehensible and seriously harms a young person who was caught in the middle of a power struggle having nothing to do with him," Abrams wrote in a statement to USA TODAY Sports. Luis declared for the 2025 NBA Draft and was in the Jazz and Celtics organizations, but joined a lawsuit to get another year of eligibility after being waived before the start of the 2025 season. Wade didn't elaborate on his decision to play Luis after Wednesday's game. "I'm going to refer to our university's statement from yesterday," he said. "I'll be happy to answer any questions about how he played, but going to refer in terms of anything about his eligibility and rostering him to the university's statement yesterday. "Everybody who played tonight is eligible." LSU went through this same situation with football, when Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris were cleared to play by the courts, added to the roster, and ultimately later removed. Expulsion talks arose during that time as well. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: LSU president orders RJ Luis benched amid SEC expulsion threat

stories.title: How the Lakers' Quentin Grimes wants to maintain his hot shooting, even off the bench
stories.summary: With Austin Reaves working toward a return to the lineup soon, Grimes and coach JJ Redick continue to look for ways to keep the guard in offensive rhythm.
stories.detailText: Lakers guard Quentin Grimes, attempting a layup against Clippers center Brook Lopez, looks to resume his hot shooting after scoring 89 points in the last three games. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) When Lakers public address announcer Derrin Horton introduced Quentin Grimes in the starting lineup Wednesday, the easy-going Lakers guard was met with an unusually loud ovation. Dropping a career-high 47 points with 10 made three-pointers less than 24 hours before warranted such a reception. Grimes has used a recent promotion to the starting lineup to fuel a career scoring binge. But his official place in the starting lineup could be short-lived when Austin Reaves returns from a left heel bruise that’s kept him sidelined for three games. No matter if Grimes gets his name announced at the beginning of the game or comes off the bench, he wants to maintain his rediscovered rhythm. “I feel like we all respect each other’s games, we know what everybody can do,” Grimes said Wednesday after he scored 20 points in the Lakers’ loss to the Utah Jazz. “JJ [Redick] gives everybody credit to go out there, no matter who it is, to be themselves, so I feel like whenever we get back whole I’ll still be able to keep playing how I’ve been playing.” The Lakers ruled Reaves out for Friday’s NBA Cup game against the Sacramento Kings at 7 p.m. at Crypto.com Arena. The guard, who was injured during the third quarter against Milwaukee on Nov. 11, did on-court work Wednesday morning before the Lakers’ game against the Jazz, and Redick said it went “well” but didn’t have any further idea about Reaves’ timeline for return. In the three games without Reaves, Grimes has flourished, averaging 29.7 points, 6.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists while shooting 57.4% from the field and 63.3% from three-point range. It’s not just the “statement” night in which he joined Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers players to make 10 or more three-pointers in a single game. In five starts this season, Grimes is averaging 24.8 points and shooting 55.3% from three compared with 5.9 points and 24% three-point shooting off the bench. The Lakers are 4-1 in games Grimes has started. Lakers guard Quentin Grimes, shooting over Jazz center Jaxson Hayes, scored 20 points on Wednesday. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times) Grimes credited his recent success to finding a rhythm after a slow start to the season in which he was eight-for-33 shooting from three in the first 11 games before missing two games because of a sprained right pinky. During his career, Grimes has averaged 14.3 points per start compared with 8.5 points coming off the bench with 59.6% and 57.8% true shooting percentage, respectively. Grimes has made a career out of shape-shifting. The 25th pick in the 2021 draft once was just trying to crack the New York Knicks rotation as a three-and-D player. With Dallas, where he played briefly with Luka Doncic, and Philadelphia, he had the ball in his hands more often, jumping between the starting lineup and the bench. Now with two dynamic scorers in Doncic and Reaves, the Lakers are searching for new ways to let Grimes shine. “A big part is like for him if he’s gonna play off-ball, he needs to feel like he’s touched the ball and he feels like he’s in a rhythm,” Redick said. “So, again, this is a new team, and we’re feeling out a bunch of stuff for each individual guy. Our job as coaches is try to maximize each player and maximize the group, and there’s a learning curve to that.” Grimes, whose relationship with Redick started in 2023 when Grimes visited Redick to work out one summer but accidentally wandered into his future coach’s neighbor’s house in the Hamptons, has cherished the open line of communication with the coaching staff. “It’s a good problem to have: a coach that wants to get you the ball, wants to get you into a rhythm, stay in that rhythm that I’ve been in,” Grimes said. “So I feel like it’s a good thing. He’s really good at what he does. We’re rolling right now. So I have no doubt he’ll be able to keep me in this rhythm once we all get healthy.” Read more: Swanson: One frigid night against the Jazz doesn't change the fact the Lakers are legit Grimes was thought to be a strong contender for an opening day starting role next to Reaves and Doncic. But the Lakers started wings Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams first along with center Walker Kessler, and then inserted 6-foot-8 forward Jake LaRavia in Williams’ place when the Lancaster native missed three games because of a left foot injury. Redick has said previously he liked the balance of those lineups: Reaves and Doncic for offensive punch, two perimeter, defensive-minded wings to back them up and hit open three-pointers and Kessler to anchor the middle. The Lakers’ lineup with Doncic, Reaves, Thybulle, LaRavia and Kessler still ranks second in net rating among five-man groups that have played more than 50 minutes together. Instead of focusing on the starting unit, Redick wants to keep tinkering with lineups to find more minutes with neither Doncic nor Reaves on the court. Coaches think those moments could help other players get into the rhythm on their own so that during the second half when the staff is deciding which lineup will finish the game, everyone will be in a good flow. “I think with this group and the way this group [is], it’s just an egoless group,” Redick said. “We’re going to be able to be flexible with the starting lineup and flexible with matchups.” Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Memphis Grizzlies showing Warriors the new generation
stories.summary: Steph Curry has outlasted two versions of the Grizzlies. Tonight the Warriors face the third without him.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 23: Cameron Boozer #27 of the Memphis Grizzlies goes up for a shot on Gary Payton II #0 of the Golden State Warriors during the first half at Chase Center on October 23, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Golden State Warriors are landing in Memphis tonight caught in a freefall, but context is everything. Steph Curry’s Dubs sent Grit and Grind home in 2015 and Ja and Jaren home in 2022. Now Memphis is on its third version, and it’s already won at Chase Center. Tonight the Warriors get their second look at these Grizzlies, this time without Steph. The timing is rough. The Grizzlies are 11-4 and fifth in the West. The Warriors (8-7) limp in on a four-game skid and the second night of a back-to-back, sitting in the last play-in spot. That skid started the night Steph left Houston with an abdominal injury that turned out to be an oblique tear . Memphis spent the last 18 months taking apart everything it had built. Grit and Grind reached the 2013 conference finals and were up 2-1 on the Warriors in 2015 before Golden State took the next three. The Ja and Jaren teams won 56 games in 2021-22, lost to the Warriors in the second round, and were done after a first-round sweep by OKC in 2025. Since then, Desmond Bane went to Orlando, Jaren Jackson Jr. went to Utah at the deadline, and in June Ja Morant was shipped to Portland for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. Coming off a 25-57 season, the Grizzlies added No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer to a young core with Cedric Coward and Zach Edey. Nobody expected much. Then they opened the season with six straight wins, and the rebuild turned into the surprise of the NBA. The face of the surprise is a familiar one. Ty Jerome, the same guy Steve Kerr called a “godsend” as a two-way player in 2022-23, went from 6.9 points per game in Golden State to leading Memphis at 25.4. In the Nov. 2 overtime loss to New Orleans he dropped 40, including 23 after the third. "He's got a full green light over there… he's a tough cover." Chef Curry gives props to the NBA's leading scorer early on, Ty Jerome, who dropped 45 PTS in Memphis' season opener, and 28 last night 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4ASqFYnNJe — NBA (@NBA) October 24, 2026 NBA-best 34.7 points per game. Second player in MEM history to score 100 points in the first three games of the season. 3-0 Grizzlies record. Ty Jerome is HOOPING hooping 🔥😮‍💨 https://t.co/i03764p1Ym pic.twitter.com/VUU86iRAPq — NBA (@NBA) October 26, 2026 Neither team will look like itself tonight. The official report has Curry out with the oblique tear, Jerome out with a right hip impingement, and Draymond Green and Zach Edey out too. That leaves two questions worth watching. Can Brandin Podziemski and Yaxel Lendeborg create enough good shots without Steph and Draymond running the offense? And without Draymond in the paint, can Golden State keep Boozer off the offensive glass? Steph has seen two versions of the Grizzlies come and go. The third already has a win at Chase. Tonight somebody else has to go into Memphis and get one back.

stories.title: Walker Kessler is confident the Lakers will bounce back strong from loss to Utah
stories.summary: Kessler is ready to learn from the defeat and move onto Friday’s game
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 18: Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers handles the ball during the game against the Utah Jazz on November 18, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Despite the Utah Jazz snapping the Los Angeles Lakers’ nine-game winning streak and dropping them to 13-3, Walker Kessler doesn’t want to dwell on the defeat for too long. With another game Friday against the Sacramento Kings, Kessler intends to quickly absorb whatever lessons he can and prepare for Sacramento, all while sounding pretty content with the process offensively Wednesday night. “It is frustrating. Tonight wasn’t our night, but I think our team is going to respond well to this loss. With 82 games, when you have a bad game like this, you don’t want to spend too much time lingering on the losses,” Kessler told reporters postgame. “You want to learn from it and move on because you have to. You have another one Friday. So our offense, as far as it not going tonight, we were getting good looks, just wasn’t falling necessarily.” Quentin Grimes, who scored 20 points on 8-of-20 shooting, feels similarly to Kessler. He believes it was a “winnable game,“ one the Lakers squandered by not meeting the precedent they’ve set this season during their 13-2 start (13-3 now). “Just not to overthink it. Tonight wasn’t our best outing for sure. It was a back to back, but we still feel like we could have won the game,” Grimes told reporters Wednesday. “I feel like if we would have made a couple more shots and just took care of the ball in two possessions and get a stop, we would have easily won the game. So it’s just a positive takeaway from it is knowing that it was a winnable game that we kind of let slip away.” Grimes, Kessler and the rest of the Lakers will look to begin a new winning streak — featuring much better shotmaking — when they welcome the Kings to Crypto.com Arena Friday at 7 p.m. They’ll also need to win this game to keep their NBA Cup Quarterfinals hopes alive since they already dropped a group stage game Oct. 30 against the Golden State Warriors. A 1-13 Sacramento squad could help them achieve that and potentially beef up their point differential — a critical tiebreaker in determining wildcard seeds. stories.title: LeBron James sues makers of 'Bron' app over unauthorized use of his nickname and AI-generated likeness
stories.summary: LeBron James is suing the makers of an app originially named "Bron," alleging they used his nickname, likeness and star power without his permission. The app was renamed on the day the complaint was filed.
stories.detailText: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James plays against the Indiana Pacers on Nov. 15. (Chris Szagola / AP Photo) Former Lakers star LeBron James is suing a company and its founders for using his nickname as the name of a sports-betting analytics app and using unauthorized AI-generated images in his likeness to advertise the product. According to a civil lawsuit filed Tuesday in U.S. District Court of New York by James and his LBJ Trademarks LLC, the San Francisco-based developer PlayVision Inc. named its app “Bron” in an attempt to benefit from James’ name and star power “without any connection between the word and Defendants or any feature of their app.” “The word ‘Bron’ has no dictionary definition and no special meaning in the context of sports analytics, wagering, or artificial intelligence,” the complaint states. “Rather, in the context of anything sports-related, it refers to only one man — LeBron James.” Read more: LeBron James says 'family is safe' after arrest of alleged stalker outside Brentwood home The Times on Thursday reached out to PlayVision and fellow defendants Anish Gupta (co-founder and CEO) and Marc Zoghby (co-founder and CTO) through the company’s email address and did not immediately receive a response. The Associated Press reports that requests for comment sent Tuesday to Gupta and Zoghby’s email accounts were also not immediately returned. In early November, PlayVision released a video advertisement for the Bron app that featured a player “with physical traits that mimic Mr. James, down to his identifiable tattoos,” according to the complaint,. The player is shown mainly from behind, with a partial side view of his face also displayed at one point, while using the app. He wears a basketball jersey that features the name “Bron” and the number 23, which is the jersey number James has worn during most of his 24 years in the NBA (including his current stint with the Philadelphia 76ers ). Read more: Swanson: One frigid night against the Jazz doesn't change the fact the Lakers are legit “The Ad catapulted the Bron App from obscurity to controversy, with the Ad gaining a million views within a day—exactly as Defendants intended,” the lawsuit states, adding, “When Mr. James’s counsel sent a cease-and-desist letter to Defendants, they used it as an opportunity to gin up additional publicity, taking down the Ad while teasing ‘a new name’ without delivering one...” On Monday, Gupta posted a video to his LinkedIn page that featured clips of people discussing and, at one point, chanting “Bron AI.” The post promoted the relaunch of the Bron app under a new name later in the week. “We found Bron. Apparently, the lawyers found it too,” Gupta wrote. “Find out our new name Wednesday. 10 AM PT.” The new app’s name, which was introduced on the same day as James’ lawsuit was filed, is “ Evie .” Read more: Stephen Curry calls out Gilbert Arenas, others over comments about wife Ayesha. Here's the latest “Defendants’ latest post underscores that Defendants’ entire marketing campaign has been in bad faith, referencing the public backlash against their Ad and daring Mr. James to sue,” the complaint states. “Defendants are not winding down their misconduct. They are milking it, stringing out the controversy one video teaser at a time for as long as it keeps the Bron App in the headlines.” The complaint lists a number of causes for action, including false endorsement, trademark infringement, false advertising, deceptive acts and practices, and violation of privacy and publicity. It seeks a jury trial and relief that includes compensatory damages, an injunction preventing the company from engaging in such activity involving James, and an order that the company informs all of the app’s users and subscribers “in writing” that James has “no affiliation with Defendants and has never used, sponsored, or endorsed the Bron App.” Get the best, most interesting and strangest stories of the day from the L.A. sports scene and beyond from our newsletter The Sports Report. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Raptors' RJ Barrett out with strained right hamstring, Collin Murray-Boyles placed in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Barrett has been dealing with a hamstring issue for the past couple of weeks, while Murray-Broyles left Tuesday's game due to illness.
stories.detailText: Toronto Raptors forward RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the team announced Thursday. Additionally, forward Collin Murray-Boyles was placed in concussion protocol as a precautionary measure. Barrett missed Wednesday's 103-99 loss to the Washington Wizards with hamstring tightness. That was the second of back-to-back games for the Raptors, who also lost to the New York Knicks on Tuesday . Barrett played 39 minutes in that game, scoring 22 points with 5 rebounds and 5 assists. However, hamstring discomfort has been an issue for Barrett in recent weeks. He has been using a stationary bike on the sideline when not on the court, in addition to during timeouts and stoppages in play, according to The Athletic's Esfandiar Baraheni . Murray-Boyles left Wednesday's contest during the first half after playing four minutes. The Raptors announced that he would not return due to illness, which has apparently been going around the team locker room. When he sustained a possible concussion is not certain. Barrett, 26, is Toronto's second-leading scorer this season, averaging 20.9 points with 6.4 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game. He's shooting a career-low 28% on 74 3-point attempts. Prior to sitting out Wednesday's contest, Barrett had appeared in all 14 of the Raptors' games. In his second season, Murray-Boyles is averaging 9.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists, in addition to 1 steal and 1.1 blocks in 14 games (eight starts). He was the Raptors' 2025 first-round pick (No. 9 overall) out of South Carolina. Toronto (5-10) has lost its past six games and eight of its past 10. The Raptors currently rank ninth in the Eastern Conference and 16th in the NBA. They visit the Detroit Pistons (10-4) on Friday.

stories.summary: Is it TImme Time Yet?
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, AZ - NOVEMBER 16: Drew Timme #2 of the Valley Suns handles the ball during the game against the Salt Lake City Stars on November 16, 2026 at Mullett Arena in Tempe, Arizona. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kate Frese/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images As we waited for the Phoenix Suns season to start, many questions arose ahead of the final decisions about the team. With them having 15 players under contract, one of them, Mark Williams, out for an extended period before the season starts, and only two centers on the roster, changes were inevitable. That is where we saw Haywood Highsmith get waived, giving the Suns flexibility with their 14-man roster, and we also saw moves on two two-way contracts. These were C.J. Huntley and Koby Brea, who were waived to add more size with Duop Reath and Drew Timme. Both Huntley and Brea remained with the Valley Suns after being waived, but they brought in two new faces who have both seen some time in the NBA. Reath spent the last three years with the Portland Trail Blazers and brings versatility to the frontcourt with his shooting. In the past, I highlighted him as a low-end free-agent target for the Suns, and I am happy to see him in the Valley this year. Even if he is just there as insurance if another big goes down, the Suns need that, and Reath can provide valuable shooting to a bench unit that already excels at that if he does get an opportunity. The name that went unnoticed, though, was Drew Timme, who joined the Suns after being waived by the Los Angeles Lakers. As with Jordan Goodwin last season, the Suns brought in someone from the Lakers, and this could prove a strategic move. After Goodwin paid off last offseason, the investment in Timme may also pay off, given his run in the G League so far. Drew Timme in G-League with @GLeagueSuns : 31 points, 12 rebounds, 7 assists, 72 FG% 34 points, 14 rebounds, 7 assists, 55 FG% 25 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 73 FG% 38 points, 10 rebounds, 6 assists, 64 FG% https://t.co/VPQezv6y53 pic.twitter.com/6u1Cl7b3OO — koa peat fan account (@FrenchValleyFR) November 17, 2026 Now, Timme is no stranger to the spotlight; he was a dominant collegiate player at Gonzaga before going undrafted in the 2023 draft. After bouncing around the Nets and Lakers, he now finds himself in the Valley with an opportunity to impress. Even though it is just the G League, these numbers prove that Timme is better than his current standing. We saw this trend with Collin Gillespie his first year in the Valley, and he turned out to be a key piece for the Suns. Timme could be that next buy-low product that the Suns invest in that pans out, and over the last few seasons, that is how they have found key depth pieces. Both Gillespie and Bouyea were on two-way contracts before landing NBA deals, and with the Suns still having that open roster spot, could that happen by the end of the season? Only time will tell if Timme gets an opportunity, but with his recent play, I wouldn’t rule it out. Especially with Mark Williams still out, the Suns lack some size in the frontcourt and have elected to give Koa Peat some small-ball minutes to replicate their third center for now. Could Timme end up fighting for that, depending on whether the Valley Suns are home? Personally, I’d like to see it. Timme, even though he hasn’t had overwhelming success in his 36 NBA games, has shown flashes of impact. Sadly, he played for a pretty poor Nets team, but with the Lakers, he made plays to help Luka Doncic and LeBron James. If you can get those quotes from the GOAT, that must mean something, right? LeBron James with some heady praise for Lakers two-way big man Drew Timme: “He’s a smart basketball player. He knows how to play the game. And his IQ correlates to this level. So it's great to see that the coaches have believed in him” pic.twitter.com/mxB9p3aQRa — Dave McMenamin (@mcten) January 21, 2026 Timme can come in and be another solid passer and playmaker in this frontcourt. Like Ighodaro, he has the basketball IQ to make not only smart plays but the right ones, and he would help open up more opportunities for those bench scorers. The team is already deep, and as a two-way player, it is not shocking that he hasn’t seen much time with the Suns yet, but if injuries open a spot, the Suns should give him that shot. This shows the Suns’ ability to build on the margins. They identify talent that can stand out, and even if it ruffles some feathers, they don’t care. They will give up on draft picks or guys who haven’t panned out if there is a better name out there, and you have to appreciate that from a business standpoint: they have gotten guys like Gillespie and Bouyea, and they only saw time with injuries. Timme’s time may relate to that, but once again he is proving, like those guys, he is better than the G League, which is what the Suns want. They need these small-impact guys to pan out and be better than anticipated to build out the bench and depth, and they’ve done that. All in all, as a fan of the team, it is nice to see them make these smart moves compared to the ones that have not worked. It shows they can succeed with these marginal moves and offers some hope that, if there is someone you don’t know who is signed to this team, they may actually pan out.

NBA Trade Lab: Dejounte Murray's trade request After formally requesting a trade last Friday , New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray has unsurprisingly been the player most involved in fan-created trades over the past seven days in our NBA Trade Lab . The Spurs traded Murray to the Hawks in 2022 for a massive haul: three first-round picks (including the Hawks' pick in the upcoming 2027 draft) and one first-round pick swap. At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In Atlanta he expanded his offensive game, but his defensive impact, as measured by Net Points , fell off a cliff. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels , who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season . Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. Let's look at some of the top fan-created trades to see what fans are thinking might be a realistic deal. Trade No. 1 Pelicans get: Jalen Green Phoenix Suns get: Dejounte Murray Green and Murray are similar in many ways, so a straight-up swap could make sense for both teams. Green is a talented scorer, but he lacks consistency and doesn't offer the ancillary skills to buoy him at a constant floor of positive impact. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg , so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system. For the Suns, this would be a bet on their system. They have built a menacing defensive identity over the past two seasons and often punch above their weight through effort and hustle. Bringing Murray into this system could help to revive some of the defensive aspects of his game that have faded in recent years. Trade No. 2 Pelicans get: Four second-round picks Charlotte Hornets get: Murray In this unusual deal, the Pelicans get no players back. It is a valid trade because of the $40 million trade exception that the Hornets received in the LaMelo Ball trade. Four second-round picks may not sound like much, but in the process the Pelicans would also open up a $32 million trade exception of their own and would completely clear Murray's money off their books without receiving any undesirable contracts in return. The Hornets' offense has been really struggling this season, ranking last in Offensive Net Points per game, after losing their offensive engine in LaMelo Ball. Trading for Murray could inject some life into their offense, strengthening their guard play while they wait for Kon Knueppel to return from injury and Coby White to return to form after a slow start to his season. Trade No. 3 Pelicans get: De'Aaron Fox and Spurs 2029 first-round pick San Antonio Spurs get: Murray and Herb Jones The Pelicans here get a proven winner and veteran presence in Fox, who could help to mentor Jeremiah Fears and their other young players throughout their roster. They also receive a 2029 first-round pick to build their future draft capital. The Spurs are rolling right now and Fox has been playing great, so this would likely be a trade they consider only if things start to go downhill a bit and they decide they want to get off Fox's contract. San Antonio might be more interested in Murray than other teams, since he played some of his best basketball there. In this deal they also receive a very valuable player in Jones, whose defensive ability could slot perfectly into the Spurs' lineups and make the Victor Wembanyama -anchored defense even more impenetrable. -- Benjamin Tiemeyer Have any more ideas on what move the Pelicans should make involving Dejounte Murray? James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."
