stories.title: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards speaks on decision to undergo knee surgery, has no clear return timeline: 'Whenever my knee tells me it's ready, then I'll be ready'
stories.summary: Edwards is set to miss multiple months after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his ailing right knee on Oct. 27.
stories.detailText: Three weeks after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his ailing knee , Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards is speaking out about his recovery. On Thursday, the guard talked to reporters for the first time since the procedure, saying that the rehabilitation process was "going great" and that he was focused on improving the strength in his leg post-surgery. Edwards also spoke about the timeline of his injury before deciding to go under the knife, saying that his knee had been bothering him on and off for years but that it had "flared up" significantly last month. "It was frustrating, but I realized I had to do it, so I just made my mind up that same day, like we're gonna do it tomorrow," Edwards said. The 25-year-old guard said that he had managed his knee well in the offseason and that it was still "good" in camp. But by the Timberwolves' season opener on Oct. 21, it was getting worse, and was "really bothering" him in the team's win over the Orlando Magic on Oct. 23. Minnesota's back-to-back on Oct. 25 and Oct. 26, against the Toronto Raptors at home and the Cleveland Cavaliers away, is when it really started to be a problem: "After the back-to-back it was really bad, like painful to fly," Edwards said. Edwards said that he hopes that the surgery will help mitigate the pain going forward. "It was something that I needed, it needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards said. "But who knows, maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else, but hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good." Edwards, who said that this is the longest he's ever gone without playing basketball, added that he plans on coming back this season but doesn't have a clear timeline. At the time of his surgery, reports indicated that he would need more than two months to recover. "I have no clue. Whenever my knee tells me it's ready, then I'll be ready," he said of a return to the court. Losing Edwards initially seemed to be a brutal blow to the Timberwolves' chances: Before the surgery, Edwards was averaging 33.3 points per game and seemed on track for another dominant season. But Minnesota has fared well in his absence, going 8-3 in the weeks since Edwards' surgery. "I was thirsty to get back, especially after the first game," Edwards said, referring to the Timberwolves' loss to the Golden State Warriors right after his procedure. "I was ready to get back and just get in their ear, tell them what I'm seeing, feel the energy. But after that game, we kinda took off, so I was like, I'll take my time. But I'm happy to be around now." While speaking to reporters, Edwards had high praise for all of his teammates, specifically pointing out the "phenomenal" play of Ayo Dosunmu — who currently leads the team in points — and noting that forward Jaden McDaniels is "stepping up big time." He also confirmed that he's been sharing his scouting reports with his teammates, staying involved in the team despite his absence from the court. Led by Dosunmu and LaMelo Ball, Minnesota is currently fourth in the Western Conference with a 11-4 record and a pretty favorable schedule over the next few weeks.

stories.title: Athletes are just as hyped for 'Grand Theft Auto VI' as everyone else
stories.summary: The latest entry in the Grand Theft Auto series is tied with "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time" with a 99 rating on Metacritic.
stories.detailText: Like (seemingly) most of the rest of the world, athletes are all-in on "Grand Theft Auto VI." The highly anticipated game was released on Thursday, 13 years after "Grand Theft Auto V," its critically acclaimed predecessor. It's more than living up to the hype -- the game is currently tied with "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time" with a 99 rating on the review aggregator Metacritic , and passed $1.8 billion in revenue on release , according to digital intelligence firm Sensor Tower's sales tracker. It's no surprise, then, that the sports world is hyped about GTA VI. Just look at what they're saying about it. Tyreek Hill Hill is actually in the game -- he's lending his voice and likeness to a fictional football player, Maleek Rivers. Erik Spoelstra The Miami Heat coach wants to play GTA VI, but he'll need one of his players to invite him over -- and he said his kids aren't allowed to play . Steven Adams The Houston Rockets center joked a few months before GTA VI's release that it could have a noticeable (negative) impact on player performance. Klay Thompson A fan since the early top-down view GTA and GTA II, Thompson was pumped for the newest game's release. Nikola Jokic Ever the iconoclast, the Denver Nuggets star isn't playing GTA VI -- but that doesn't mean he avoids gaming entirely. Jokic said he'll be playing League of Legends on his phone.

stories.title: Anthony Edwards: 'I never wanted to have surgery,' no timeline for return
stories.summary: When will Ant return? "I have no clue. Whenever my knee tells me it's ready, I'll be ready."
stories.detailText: Oct 25, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards (5) looks on against the Toronto Raptors in the second half at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Anthony Edwards met with the media Thursday, but that doesn't mean he'll be back on the court later that night when the Timberwolves host the Knicks. When will he return? "I have no clue. Whenever my knee tells me it's ready, I'll be ready," Edwards said in his first public words since he had arthroscopic surgery to clean up his right knee three weeks ago. The surgery is expected to keep Ant sidelined until around Christmas. Edwards said he didn't really want to have the surgery, but had to after the pain got worse. "I'm the type of guy, I never wanted to have surgery. I thought it would just, you know, go away. In the offseason it was actually good, like we was managing it pretty good, treating it, and it wasn't as swole. Then, as soon as the season kicked off it, I don't know what happened. It just flared back up like really bad. Then I was like, "Man, it's time"... "It was good in [training] camp, like I said. I think after the Miami game it started to flare up, and then it went down a little bit after the Orlando game, so we thought we were going to be alright, but then after the back-to-back it was really bad, like painful to fly, so I'm like, "I gotta get it." It's a small sample size, but Edwards arguably was playing the best basketball of his career to start the season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game while shooting 40% from 3-point range, all while the Timberwolves were 3-1. Minnesota, behind LaMelo Ball, Ayo Dosunmu and the best defense in the league, has gone 5-2 since Edwards went out. Edwards recognized what is going on and said that when he returns he wants to fit in. "I'm thirsty to come back, but not super fast because of how they're playing. I don't want to take them out of rhythm," Edwards said. "But I told them, when I come back, I'm not going to try to be who I usually am and try to ball hog and take all the shots. I'm just going to fit in where I get in – take a couple catch-and-shoots. When they need me, I'm there." Edwards isn't just going to accept a role, he's an elite player, but Minnesota might be better — and a more dangerous playoff team — because of what they have learned while he is out.

stories.title: Luka Dončić says fatigue can’t be an excuse for Lakers loss to Jazz
stories.summary: Dončić took responsibility for his poor play and said he has “to do way better” as a leader on the team
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 18: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts as he walks back to the bench during a 109-97 Utah Jazz win at Crypto.com Arena on November 18, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Playing their third game in four nights, the Los Angeles Lakers saw their nine-game winning streak come to an end Wednesday when they fell at home to the Utah Jazz, 109-97. Plenty of players struggled, including the Lakers’ franchise superstar, Luka Dončić , who tallied 29 points on 10-of-28 shooting (2-of-12 from deep), seven assists and nine turnovers. Following the loss, Dončić took accountability for his lackluster game and refused to let tired legs be the reason behind Los Angeles’ poor performance. “That can’t be an excuse. All NBA team plays 82 games, so that can’t be an excuse,” Dončić said. “I got to do way better. I know that. I feel like we had some open shots we didn’t make, but it’s one game. We got to move on.” Dončić’s 10-of-28 shooting (35.7%) marked his worst field goal percentage of the year while his 29 points were his fewest since Oct. 23 and his nine turnovers were his second-most this season. If the Lakers are going to contend for a championship like they aspire to, their best player, who rarely has this year, cannot sink to that level — and he knows it. “I mean, honestly, I just got to be way better than this, Dončić said. ”This is unacceptable for my part. I’ve got to lead the team in better ways. I look at this game, got to move on and learn from this.” Dončić’s head coach, JJ Redick, refused to single out one player for the loss Wednesday. Dončić may be their superstar and most impactful contributor but he was far from the lone guy to play significantly below the standard they’ve set for themselves this season. “I asked the guys, ‘Who in here feels like they played well tonight?’ Nobody raised their hand. Everybody could be better,” Redick told reporters postgame. “We can sit here and nitpick every single guy. Nitpick me. It’s whatever. Could my rotations have been different? Maybe [could have] gotten a little more offense, maybe played a little more size at the five when Jaxson [Hayes] or [Mo] Bamba was [out there]? Yeah. We’ll do all that, but we didn’t play well. Nobody played well. It’s not Walker, it’s not Luka, it’s not Q, it’s not Sandro. Nobody had a great game.” You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory
stories.summary: The Sixers wiped out a 17-point deficit and earned a shorthanded win Wednesday night over the Magic.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers come back for strong shorthanded victory originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stretched their winning streak to four games and snagged a strong road win Wednesday night over the Magic. They earned a 121-116 victory in Orlando to improve to 13-3 on the season. The Magic dropped to 6-8. Joel Embiid had 26 points, seven assists, six rebounds, three blocks and two steals. VJ Edgecombe posted a season-high 24 points, eight boards and six assists. LeBron James scored 22 points and Anfernee Simons added 18. Magic star Franz Wagner had 27 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds. The Sixers had a long injury list in Orlando. Tyrese Maxey (right foot soreness), Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain) and Dean Wade (left hamstring soreness/tightness) were among their players out. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters in Orlando that Brown will be re-evaluated when the team returns to Philadelphia. Orlando was without star forward Paolo Banchero (right high ankle sprain). The Sixers will start a three-game homestand when they face the Bucks on Saturday afternoon. Here are observations on their win over the Magic: New starting five struggles early The Sixers’ undermanned starting lineup was Edgecombe, Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid. After scoring 37 points in the Sixers’ win over the Nets , Embiid had a subpar start. He began 1 for 6 from the floor and committed a turnover that led to an Anthony Black dunk. The Sixers’ lineup looked exactly like a unit that hadn’t built any chemistry yet. The team was not sharp early on either end of the floor. Desmond Bane drained a long three-pointer to give Orlando a 27-12 advantage. Orlando made 11 of its first 14 field goals and led by as many as 17 points in the first quarter. Expanded bench has bright night Labaron Philon Jr. and Justin Edwards joined the Sixers’ rotation. So did two-way contract players Tacko Fall and Caleb Love. Philon impressed in the first quarter, converting two floaters and a corner three. The rookie passed his previous NBA scoring high of five points and finished the night with 10 on 4-for-5 shooting. Fall played 10 minutes and posted two points, three rebounds and three blocks. He slammed in a dunk and rejected two shots early in the second quarter. Credit to Fall for giving the Sixers a good backup center performance and doing his job as a rim-protecting ultra-big man. Love entered in the second quarter and was ready to fire, hitting a catch-and-shoot three-pointer on his first touch. The Sixers’ zone defense also helped them eat into the Magic’s lead. The zone seemed to disrupt Orlando’s offensive rhythm and it was active enough to prevent the Magic from consistently creating high-quality looks. Edgecombe’s buzzer-beating mid-range jumper cut the Sixers’ deficit to 69-64 after two quarters. Still perfect in the clutch The Sixers pulled within a single point on multiple occasions in the third quarter, including on a Philon three late in the period. They trailed by five points after the third. Fall continued to play well early in the fourth quarter. He deterred the Magic’s drivers from getting all the way to the rim as the very large back line of the Sixers’ zone defense and made eye-catching hustle plays on both sides of the ball. The Sixers outscored Orlando by seven points on the night with Fall on the court. Soon after Embiid subbed back in, he evened the game at 104-all with two free throws. Jabari Walker swished a three to finally push the Sixers in front. The Magic regained a late lead with a Jalen Suggs three. James then drove and kicked the ball out to Edgecombe, who nailed one of his customary clutch jumpers to put the Sixers back on top. No matter the night-to-night personnel, the Sixers have been fantastic at the tail end of close games. They’re now 11-0 in clutch situations , which the NBA defines as games within a five-point differential in the final five minutes.

stories.title: How LeBron James dissected Pacers defense down the stretch
stories.summary: James might not be the elite bucket-getter he once was, but he can still conduct highly-efficient offense.
stories.detailText: How LeBron James dissected Pacers defense down the stretch originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia As he overtook Jason Kidd for the third-most assists in NBA history , LeBron James piloted the Sixers’ offense down the stretch against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday. With Joel Embiid sitting out and Tyrese Maxey getting a breather on the bench, James took over in the fourth quarter. He did so by spamming the same action over and over again. The set consisted of James getting a ball screen from a guard – either VJ Edgecombe or Anfernee Simons – at the top of the key. After setting or ghosting the screen, the guard would short roll towards the basket. When the Pacers blitzed or hedged the screen, James found the guard. The Sixers could then attack a 4-on-3 or 3-on-2 situation. Twice, Edgecombe and Simons scored off the roll. When the Pacers helped to the roller, that opened up the shooters in each corner. James directed traffic on offense to ensure that the Sixers spaced the floor properly. Here, he waved Dean Wade out of the dunker spot and into the corner. Edgecombe promptly hit him for an open three off the short roll. After all of the Sixers’ success, the Pacers eventually switched the ball screen. That left the 6-foot-4, 173-pound Quenton Jackson on James, who has five inches and 77 pounds on him. Jackson and James had already gone head to head on Sunday. In the first quarter, James set a ball screen for Edgecombe which the Pacers switched. Edgecombe fed James in the post and the Pacers doubled him to support Jackson. James punished them for it. They didn’t double James after the switch in the fourth quarter. This time, James backed Jackson down, backed him down again and backed him down some more before scoring inside. James’ strength abusing matchups against smaller defenders after switches has been a safety valve for the Sixers’ offense. Guards struggle to stop him from getting to the basket. When defenses send help, he picks them apart with his otherworldly passing ability. That combination forced the Pacers to pick their poison. From the 9:55 mark in the fourth until the Pacers switched to a zone defense (after James bullied Jackson) with just over 6:00 left, the Sixers scored 13 points out of this action across seven possessions. That’s a stellar 1.86 points per possession. James, who’s scoring a career-low 15.1 points per game so far this season, might not be the elite bucket-getter he was for most of his career. But he’s still brilliant at conducting highly efficient offense that pressures a defense’s pain points. View this post on Instagram

stories.title: Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return
stories.summary: PG-13, the former Sixer, poured in 36 points, then explained the baseline exchange that gave his return an R rating.
stories.detailText: Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia PG-13 was rated R in his return to Philadelphia. The middle finger Paul George directed toward one baseline fan only reinforced that rating. Tuesday night was expected to revolve around Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum sharing an NBA court as opponents for the first time. Instead, the other headliner in the summer’s blockbuster trade stole the show. George scored a game-high 36 points in Boston’s 123-101 win over the Sixers. He shot 14 for 22 from the floor, made six of his 11 three-point attempts and scored 14 consecutive Boston points in the fourth quarter. The game was tied at 79 with 3:19 remaining in the third quarter. Boston outscored Philadelphia 44-22 from that point forward. The Celtics went nine minutes and 20 seconds without making a two-point field goal during the second half. Instead, they made nine consecutive field goals from three, the second-longest such streak by a Sixers opponent over the last 30 seasons. Payton Pritchard opened the fourth with consecutive threes. George followed with eight straight points, helping the Celtics begin the quarter on a 14-0 run that turned a competitive game into a rout. George’s return carried a complicated history. His two seasons with the Sixers were repeatedly interrupted by injuries, but he also played a significant role in their most memorable playoff run in years. Last spring, George helped the Sixers overcome a 3-1 deficit to eliminate Boston in seven games. He averaged 17.4 points and shot 55 percent from three during the series. Tyrese Maxey was happy to see his former teammate Tuesday, even if he disliked what followed. “It was good to see Paul,” Maxey said. “I love him, love his family. … He gave us everything he had while he was here. We know what he did in the playoffs last year. Great person, great family, and we’ll see him again.” Maxey then added one important qualifier. “I wanted him to score zero points.” George instead scored from nearly everywhere. “He had some open threes. He had some pull-up threes. He had some middies,” Maxey said. “He played within the game, too. That’s what Paul does. He plays within the game. He takes what the defense gives him, and we gave him too many open looks tonight. “PG, we know what PG does. We shouldn’t even be allowing him to get up 11 threes, and that’s on us.” Nick Nurse watched George attack the Sixers in several ways. “He really had it going,” Nurse said. “He’d post up, and-one, fallaways. He went down the lane, high archer off the glass, and-one. He scored in about every way he could tonight.” George heard boos during his return and said the arena carried the atmosphere, though not quite the intensity, of a playoff game. “This building can be very electric as well,” George said. “It was fun. It was fun to play in this environment.” One interaction extended beyond the usual reception for a returning player. During a stoppage, the ball rolled toward a fan seated along the baseline. George said the fan looked directly at him before dropping the ball instead of returning it. “There was a fan being an a–,” George said. “The ball rolled to him. He looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if I’m a dog to go fetch or go get it, instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do. “And so, yeah, then I rolled him a middle finger in return.”

stories.title: ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround
stories.summary: Nick Nurse installed a new action hours before tip-off. The Sixers returned to it late to create open looks for LeBron James and Anfernee Simons.
stories.detailText: ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers created their two cleanest late-game looks several hours before they needed them. During Wednesday morning’s shootaround in Orlando, Nick Nurse had the Sixers work on offensive material they had not consistently used this season. They tested one of those actions during the first half, returned to it throughout the closing minutes and watched it produce the shots they needed to complete a 17-point comeback. “We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn’t used before, and they ran all that stuff very, very well and very calmly and with composure,” Nurse told reporters. The Sixers have earned six of their 13 wins after trailing by double digits. They are also 11-0 in games that reached clutch time. Relying on comebacks is not a sustainable plan. The repeated late-game situations, however, have forced a new roster to respond to different lineups, coverages and responsibilities while the season is still young. Each close finish gives Nurse more information about which players and actions hold up when possessions tighten. Wednesday gave him a new option. Anfernee Simons’ clinching three in the Sixers’ 121-116 win over the Magic was the final result of that preparation. “That last play, we ran that play in the first half,” Simons said. “We worked it a couple of times, and in the second half we ran that play every single time down the stretch, and it worked every time. “It was a play we ran through. [It’s gratifying] especially when it’s working consistently and you’re getting different shots out of it and the opposing team just don’t know what to do. “We just continue to run the play and get the open shots we need.” The set is called Horns Chin. NBC Sports Philadelphia video producer and Sixers Talk podcast co-host Kevin Rice broke down how the Sixers used its different options to keep Orlando guessing. The action begins with two players stationed near the elbows. A player on the opposite elbow then sets a screen for the player up top, who receives the ball while moving around it. The Sixers ran the set three consecutive times during the first half. None of the possessions reached the primary option. Each still produced a quality opportunity. On the first, Joel Embiid cleared LeBron James out of the area and directed Simons around him for a dribble handoff. Simons received an open three-point look. Orlando took away the handoff the next time down but left Embiid one-on-one against Wendell Carter Jr. Embiid created enough room to retrieve his own miss and convert an and-one opportunity. The third attempt pulled Orlando’s defense into the paint. Two passes moved the ball through the collapsing coverage and created an open three for VJ Edgecombe. View this post on Instagram “We had a little thing where he comes flying off behind Joel, and he doesn’t get to do that that much, right?” Nurse said of Simons. “So tonight he gets the opportunity to do it, and it was very good for us on a number of plays.” The Sixers changed the action late without abandoning its initial Horns alignment. Simons moved through the lane to help form a Spain pick-and-roll involving James and Embiid. On the first late possession, Simons remained near the play after James gained a matchup against Carter. Orlando struggled to sort out its assignments, leaving James open for a 19-foot jumper with 54.8 seconds remaining. James made it a two-possession game. After Jalen Suggs made one of two free throws, the Sixers returned to the same setup. This time, Simons relocated to the left corner after James drew Carter on a switch. James drove into the paint. Suggs lost track of Simons while responding to the penetration, and James sent the ball toward the corner. Simons buried the open three to give the Sixers a 119-113 lead with 15 seconds left. “Bron just penetrated the paint,” Simons said. “It kind of got some confusion, and when I was on the dunker and kind of spaced out to the corner, I ended up finding myself wide open for the three, and Bron found me.” The Sixers entered the night without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, their two leading scorers. Simons made his first start with Philadelphia and recorded 18 points in the city where he grew up. His final basket also illustrated why Nurse believes the Sixers have more to uncover with him. “When he’s out there, they gotta be really careful,” Nurse said. “So I think there’s some drives he creates, and just about every time he lets it go, whether he’s on balance or not, you think it’s going in, and that is a big deal. Like, that is a big deal. “And again, I think we’re still a ways away from really unlocking him to being even more part of some of the things we can do with him to create more shots.” Philadelphia is now 11-0 in clutch games. The finish in Orlando provided a more specific explanation than experience or shot-making alone. The Sixers installed a set in the morning, explored its counters and trusted it when the game tightened. James supplied the patience to read Orlando’s coverage. Embiid occupied the middle of the action. Simons moved without the ball, and Edgecombe remained ready to shoot. James said his heart rate drops when close games increase the pressure on everyone else. “I mean, experience,” James said. “A guy that’s seen every situation this league has to offer. It’s nothing I haven’t seen. And, you know, in the moments where people’s heart rate goes up or anxiety goes up, mine is pretty low. It’s actually lower, you know.” The Sixers still have more actions and reads to learn as Nurse becomes familiar with his new personnel, but their latest win showed their innate ability to adapt in big moments. “I think we’re still a long ways away from knowing all the reads and all that stuff because it’s just a little early, right?” Nurse said.

stories.title: Sixers rule Brown out with hamstring injury for Magic game
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown will miss the Sixers' game Wednesday night against the Magic.
stories.detailText: Sixers rule Brown out with hamstring injury for Magic game originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown will miss his second game as a Sixer on Wednesday night when the team meets the Magic in Orlando. The Sixers listed Brown as out with a left hamstring strain on their Tuesday evening injury report. Brown had a head-to-head collision with Julius Randle in the fourth quarter of the Sixers’ win Monday over the Nets. He returned after a few minutes of game action with a bandage on his forehead, but Brown exited again with 1:44 left and did not re-enter. Brown’s only other absence this season came in an Oct. 30 victory vs. the Knicks because of left knee patellar tendinopathy. He scored 31 points in both games of the Sixers’ latest back-to-back. For the season, the five-time All-Star wing has averaged 22.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists. Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) , Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) all remain out for the 12-3 Sixers. stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.title: LeBron Log No. 5: Popcorn in hand, a viral chorus and ‘basketball AI'
stories.summary: James reached third on the NBA’s career assists list, disputed an ESPN report and stayed busy during a night off in Brooklyn.
stories.detailText: LeBron Log No. 5: Popcorn in hand, a viral chorus and ‘basketball AI' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James spent Monday night in street clothes. He still managed to argue a call with popcorn in his hand, practice his golf swing during a timeout and reject a report about himself before the Sixers left Brooklyn with a win. That followed a Sunday afternoon in which James passed Jason Kidd on the NBA’s career assists list and received an unusual description from Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle. Welcome to the fifth edition of the LeBron Log. POPCORN AND A DENIAL James sat out the Sixers’ 135-123 win over the Nets because of low back and sciatica management. It was his fourth absence through 15 games. James has yet to play both ends of a back-to-back this season after logging nearly 33 minutes Sunday against Indiana. He watched Monday’s game from the end of the Sixers’ bench in a yellow hat and an “Ohio Baby” sweatshirt. James snacked from a small bag before switching to popcorn. When Joel Embiid believed he was fouled on a first-half drive, James stood and pleaded his case to official Jacyn Goble without putting down the box. He also joined conversations between teammates and officials during several timeouts. James found another way to pass a third-quarter stoppage. As “Hot To Go” played inside Barclays Center, he practiced his golf swing near the bench. His most pointed contribution came on Instagram. An ESPN story by Dave McMenamin cited a Sixers source who said James had asked the coaching staff to remain patient while he worked toward finding his rhythm and conditioning by December. James reposted ESPN’s graphic and rejected the account. “🧢! Those words never came out of my mouth!” he wrote. The Sixers improved to 4-0 without James. They have beaten the Bucks, Hornets, Raptors and Nets in the games he has missed. 10-0, AGAIN Brooklyn pulled within five points during the final five minutes Monday, putting the Sixers in another clutch game. They have won all 10 this season. Philadelphia has reached 10 clutch wins more quickly than almost any team since the statistic began being tracked in 1996-97. The 2026-27 Sixers are the second team in that span with at least 10 such victories through their first 15 games. The other was the 1997-98 Atlanta Hawks, who had 12. James was also on the last team before Philadelphia to open a season with at least 10 consecutive clutch wins. The Lakers started 13-0 in those games last season. James did not play in the Sixers’ latest close finish, but he has now been part of the last two teams to start at least 10-0 under those circumstances. ‘BASKETBALL AI’ Before Sunday’s game, Carlisle explained why he tries to limit his play calls against James. “LeBron James is one of the reasons we try not to have play calls, ’cause he knows all of them,” Carlisle said. “He’s a walking NBA basketball AI machine. That’s what he is.” James followed with 15 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds in the Sixers’ 131-124 win. His pass to VJ Edgecombe for a layup with 1:19 remaining gave him 12,092 career assists and moved him past Kidd for third in NBA history. Only Chris Paul and John Stockton remain ahead of him. Noah Levick wrote more about James’ milestone and the anticipation behind his passes . When told what Carlisle had called him, James appreciated the description. “So, yeah, Rick is great,” James said. “He’s one of the greatest coaches of all time, and I’ve had my battles with him over the years. That’s super humbling coming from a guy like that.” PLAY THE SONG Philadelphia has found its soundtrack for James’ biggest home moments. The Sixers have played the viral “LeBron, LeBron, LeBron” song after several of his baskets, including his late putback against the Knicks on Oct. 30. The refrain comes from a version of Steve Lacy’s “Oh Yeah?” that replaces “Come on” with James’ name. The Baylor University Men’s Choir performed its own rendition , helping the song spread across social media. Lacy later joined in. During an Oct. 15 concert at Freedom Mortgage Pavilion in Camden, he performed the LeBron version as the crowd sang along. James has noticed Philadelphia’s use of it. “I’ve seen it. I’ve heard it. It’s pretty hilarious, to be honest,” James said. “I heard it towards the end of a game when we were winning. I made a play, and I heard that song. I was just chuckling to myself on the inside.”

stories.title: Timberwolves' Edwards has 'no clue' on when he will return
stories.summary: Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards said he has "no clue" when he will return to play from right knee surgery weeks ago, but was optimistic about his long-term prognosis.
stories.detailText: Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards said he has "no clue" when he will return to play from the right knee surgery he had weeks ago, but he was optimistic about his long-term prognosis and the Timberwolves season to date. "I plan on coming back, but I don't know when," he said following Timberwolves shootaround Thursday morning as they prepared to play the Knicks later in the evening. "I'm just trying to get my strength back in my leg. I think that's the most difficult part." He didn't want to estimate if it would be weeks or months regarding his return, being careful to temper expectations. Last season, Edwards missed 21 games with an assortment of injuries, the first time he's played fewer than 72 games in a season. Before last season, he played in 79 games in each season from 2023 to '25. Edwards was off to a torrid start to the season, with two 40-point games in the first four, but the pain in his right knee was increasing. Following a 47-point performance against Cleveland on Oct. 26, he said he made the decision "that day" to have the procedure. He said his knee was pretty swollen the night before, when they played the Toronto Raptors -- he scored 26 points nonetheless. "It needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards said. "But who knows? Maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else. But hopefully not. I think I think I'll be pretty good." Edwards appeared in good spirits, smiling and joking about giving his teammates scouting reports in group chats the day of games. "I feel like the reason I wake up every morning is for competition, to compete, and I can't compete," Edwards said. "So I might as well just send them what I'm thinking every time we got a game. I'll just send a long scouting report on what guys like to do, don't like to do." He avoided surgery in the offseason, believing he wouldn't have to undergo any procedure at all. But in the opening weeks, it became an issue. "I'm the type of guy, I never wanted to have surgery. Like I thought it would just go away," Edwards said. "In the offseason, it was actually good. Like we was managing it pretty good, treating it, and it wasn't as [swollen], and then like soon the season kicked off. I don't know what happened. It just flared back up like really bad, and then I was like, man, it's time." The Timberwolves have played well in his absence, their 11-4 record placing them in the top four in the Western Conference. Edwards credits new teammate LaMelo Ball for the team's style and effectiveness. "I think we got a lot of unselfish players on the team," Edwards said. "We got seven, eight guys that that put their ego to the side and just care about winning, and I think LaMelo drives that because he brings like this pass-first mentality. I think he's super impactful on the offensive end." When he does come back, it could make the Timberwolves even more dangerous in the Western Conference. Edwards said he won't be disruptive to the way they're playing. "I'm thirsty to come back, but not super fast. I don't want to take them out of rhythm," Edwards said. "But I told them like when I come back, I'm not gonna try to be you know who I usually am. Try to ball hog and take all the shots, but you know I'm just gonna fit in where I get in. But I ain't gonna do too much." When asked how he could score 47 despite his knee pain, he chuckled: "When you can shoot the ball really good, that helps."

teamStories.title: Sources: Spurs' Dylan Harper out 1-3 weeks with hip strain
teamStories.summary: Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday.
teamStories.detailText: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday. This type of strain will carry a one-to-three-week timetable for return, dependent on Harper's rehab. Harper was injured when he appeared to slip on a wet spot in the team's 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons in San Antonio on Tuesday night. Harper writhed on the floor in pain after the play and appeared to grab at his groin area. "The visuals and optics of falls, potential injuries, whatever you want to call it can be impressionable. And that one did not look great," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "So, there's a lot of WebMD and you try not to let your mind run the wrong way and you hope for the best," he continued. "But you really don't know. It's part of the things we can't control. So, we're just very lucky, fortunate and mostly just happy for Dylan that there will be some time [that he's out]. Very best case scenario for a lot of the things that could have been." Teammates Keldon Johnson and David Jones Garcia initially escorted Harper to the tunnel before the second-year guard put his arm over the shoulder of a staffer who helped him down the hallway. Harper is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 15 games this season.

After further testing, the San Antonio Spurs have diagnosed guard Dylan Harper with a left hip external rotator strain, a story first reported by Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News . He clearly was in pain and stayed down while play continued on the other end, and he was eventually helped off the court and back to the locker room. Dylan Harper just went down in San Antonio Looks like a groin injury after planting and slipping. pic.twitter.com/NgaMD5aTBL — SpursRΞPORTΞR (@SpursReporter) November 18, 2026 Harper, 20, has taken a step forward this season, averaging 18.4 points on 50.5% shooting, plus 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game, while playing high-level defense — he might already be the second-best Spurs player. teamStories.title: Dylan Harper avoids serious hip injury in relief to Spurs
teamStories.summary: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has a left hip rotator strain and is expected to miss one to three weeks, according to reports.
teamStories.detailText: Dylan Harper's feet went out from under him with a little more than a minute left, and for a few long minutes it looked like the San Antonio Spurs ' red-hot start might go down with him. Turns out the Spurs caught a break. Harper has a left hip rotator strain and avoided a major injury, both ESPN and the San Antonio Express-News reported . He is expected to miss from one to three weeks. The second-year guard got hurt late in the Spurs' 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Nov. 17. With 1:07 left, Harper stopped to plant on a pass from Stephen Castle , and his feet slid out from under him on what appeared to be a wet spot on the court. Detroit's Ausar Thompson picked off the pass while Harper stayed on the floor, grabbing at his groin. Dylan Harper splits and lands awkwardly at the end of the 4th quarter, and he is in immense pain due to a non-contact injury. He was helped to the locker room. With replays. Spurs and NBC commentary. You can also hear Harper saying stuff at the end of the second broadcast (NBA) pic.twitter.com/UNPWKvbkW7 — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 18, 2026 He was down for about a minute before a Spurs foul stopped play. Teammates and staff had to help him off the court. He had 20 points, four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes before he left. The loss ended San Antonio's 12-game winning streak. The way the Spurs talked after the game, they seemed braced for a long absence. Two days later, the mood has changed. The San Antonio Express News reported that Harper walked into the shootaround before Thursday's game against the Los Angeles Clippers without a limp. The Spurs had already ruled out Harper for the Nov. 19 game against the Clippers because of left hip soreness. It's the first game he has missed this season. He had started and played in all 15 games alongside De'Aaron Fox and Castle in the backcourt. The Spurs are 12-3 and second in the Western Conference, and Harper has been a big reason why. The No. 2 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists while shooting 50.5% from the field. What does Dylan Harper's injury mean for the Spurs? This comes as a dose of good news. The Spurs are talented and deep enough to remain competitive in Harper's absence, especially because of San Antonio's depth at guard. Harper, 20, had been in the middle of a breakout season, his first as a starter, and has become one of the more promising young players in the NBA. He excels in transition and does not shy away from getting to the rim, which helps open up space for San Antonio's perimeter shooters, so it's not like his absence won't be felt. But the Spurs can actually return to the starting lineup that led them to an NBA Finals appearance last season, with Julian Champagnie sliding into small forward to replace Harper. If Harper remains sidelined past the return of Tobias Harris (calf), that would give San Antonio further flexibility, as Harris is a floor-spacing forward known for his perimeter shooting. Harris is yet to make his Spurs debut, but he would mitigate the loss of Harper, albeit in a very different way. And while the Spurs love the contributions of Keldon Johnson , they prefer him to come off the bench as the sixth man; don't expect that to change. All to say: San Antonio should be breathing a sigh of relief because the continued development of Harper is necessary for any championship run. stories.title: C.J. Stroud connects with Nico Collins to give Texans 7-3 lead
stories.summary: The Texans were outplayed for most of the first quarter, but they have a 7-3 lead.
stories.detailText: The Texans were outplayed for most of the first quarter, but they have a 7-3 lead. Spencer Shrader kicked a 34-yard field but missed from 56, giving the Colts an early 3-0 lead. They had drives of nine plays, 44 yards and eight plays, 35 yards. The Colts defense, missing cornerbacks Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, intercepted C.J. Stroud on the Texans' first drive. It was a fluke pick, first hitting AJ Haulcy in the helmet, then off the hands of Cam Bynum before landing back in Haulcy's hands. The Texans, though, answered on their second drive. Stroud avoided the blitz of cornerback Kapena Gushiken, who grabbed a piece of Stroud's jersey, by stepping up in the pocket before heaving a dime into the end zone to Nico Collins. stories.title: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich takes blame for ugly touchdown drought
stories.summary: It has been a long nine quarters for the Jets offense, which hasn’t scored a touchdown since the Nov. 1 loss to the Raiders in Las Vegas.
stories.detailText: New York Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich speaks to the media before practice in Florham Park, N.J., Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. It has been a long nine quarters for the Jets offense, which hasn’t scored a touchdown since the Nov. 1 loss to the Raiders in Las Vegas . Take flight with the Jets Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off. tRY IT NOW Few have felt the impact of the drought more than offensive coordinator Frank Reich. “It starts with me,’’ Reich said Thursday. “I’m the offensive coordinator. I — and we as a staff — have to put players in position to do what they do. We’ve got a very talented group. We need to do a better job coaching [and] the players need to do their part in executing and making plays.” The Jets have been held to eight Jason Sanders field goals since finding the end zone against the Raiders. “We know we need to put more points on the board, whether it’s in the red zone or whether we’re farther out, we still want to be explosive,’’ Reich said. “It’s been nine quarters. Believe me, I feel every play of that nine quarters.” Offensive coordinator Frank Reich speaks to the media before Jets practice on Nov. 19, 2026, in Florham Park, N.J. Bill Kostroun for NYPost Among the criticism of the Jets offense has been an inability to get the team’s playmakers involved enough on offense. “When your record is what it is and you go nine quarters without scoring a touchdown, that’s what we’re here all hours of the day trying to get right,’’ Reich said. “We’re working hard to get that right, and I’m confident we will.” Geno Smith (ankle) was limited in practice Thursday, but was on the field during warmups and has said he expects to play. If Smith can’t go, Cade Klubnik would be called upon again after filling in for Smith in Sunday’s loss to the Bills . Klubnik — who went 11-for-20 for 137 yards and one interception and was sacked three times in his NFL debut — was asked what he thought after having some time to watch film. Quarterback Cade Klubnik runs up field during the Jets’ Week 10 blowout loss to the Bills at MetLife Stadium. AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura “There were some good things,’’ Klubnik said. “I made some good throws with confidence, and I was happy with some of my checks and my presence was calm.” Perhaps most importantly, he didn’t feel overmatched. His teammates agreed he looked the part, which tells the fourth-round pick out of Clemson that he’s headed in the right direction. “I think it showed my preparation has been good,’’ Klubnik said. “I’ll be able to keep that going, whether I start or not [this week]. It feels good because I didn’t finish the game and come home and say the next morning, ‘I wish I did something completely different.’ The process was good, but always needs to be fine-tuned.” Add Demario Davis to the chorus of people praising rookie David Bailey , who has 7 ½ sacks and five forced fumbles just nine games into his career. “He’s had unreal progression,’’ Davis said Thursday of the No. 2 overall pick. “To be at the top of the league in sacks and pressures is impressive.’’ And Davis has also liked what he’s seen in other aspects of Bailey’s game, like his ability to affect attempted screens and deflect passes. CHECK OUT THE LATEST NFL STANDINGS AND JETS STATS “He’s able to do all facets,’’ Davis said. “You wouldn’t know he was a rookie.” Andrew Beck, a fullback, has kicked off 10 times as the Jets look for an advantage in their coverage game, using him as a potential added tackler. Special teams coach Chris Banjo noted that since teams are still adjusting to the new kickoff rules, “the challenge as coaches is to find that extra edge …” Wide receivers Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) didn’t practice.

stories.title: Kyren Williams hopes GTA VI release distracts other NFL teams
stories.summary: The release of Grand Theft Auto could be a distraction, Kyren Williams hopes not for the Rams
stories.detailText: Kyren Williams made it clear that he does not want the massive release of Grand Theft Auto VI to be a distraction to the Los Angeles Rams as they prepare for perhaps their biggest game of the year against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12, and go from there. Williams was asked on ESPN how the trendy release of GTA VI could or would impact the Rams? Williams responded during the interview with laughter and glee at the thought of the game coming out, and he confessed to Peter Schrager that he hopes he and his teammates stay focused on winning, while taking some healthy time to away from football to check out the new video game. On the flip side, Williams hopes other NFL teams play the new game all day, all night and twice on Sunday. Said Williams on the release of GTA VI during L.A.’s bye week: “I hope it impacts everybody, but the Rams, you know? And so, I hope the Rams, I hope my teammates and I are able to game a little bit, but still, you know, get to bed and be on time for practice and you know be alert and whatnot. But I am super excited. I’m glad that you brought that up cause I gotta go pre-load it, I gotta go pre-download it, you know, when we get done here. But yah I’m super excited for GTA and we’re on a bye week, so it’s like, bro this is the best week ever.” NFL players across the league and people all over the world have been waiting for the pop culture phenomena that is the new Grand Theft Auto, and it’s releasing in the thick of the NFL season. Cleveland Browns’ quarterback Deshaun Watson was asked about the playoffs and the Browns chances . Watson gave the classic answer about taking it “one game at a time” before basically stating that at this point in the season, players are thinking more about the new Grand Theft Auto than playoffs . And to be fair, playoffs are still a while off while GTA VI is out now. Keep your feet where they are. "Coach don't even mention it … we're not getting ahead of ourselves. Most of the guys are thinking about GTA, for real." Browns QB Deshaun Watson on if him and his teammates are thinking about the playoffs 😅 (via @FredGreetham9 ) pic.twitter.com/dBMpg48aGW — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 18, 2026 Of course, players like Williams and Watson do have a few million reasons to put down the controller and stick with the football. While many gamers all over will be celebrating, gamers like Williams and others are in the busy part of their work season. And gamers like Williams hope they can stay focused on football and a potential Super Bowl run now, and focus on Grand Theft Auto later. Ask any gamer, focusing on the task at hand while worrying about a new game later: Easier said than done. We’ll see how Williams and the Rams do. Game on.

stories.title: Panthers aim to hold NFC South lead while Ravens look to keep playoffs hopes alive, end 5-game skid
stories.summary: — The Carolina Panthers needed a walk-off 54-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald to beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 last Sunday and remain in first...
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — The Carolina Panthers needed a walk-off 54-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald to beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 last Sunday and remain in first place in the NFC South. Now the goal is finding a way to stay there. The Baltimore Ravens (4-6), on the other hand, are simply looking to win a game when they travel to Charlotte, North Carolina, to face the Panthers (4-5) on Sunday. The Ravens have lost five straight, including a 23-20 defeat to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night after being bullied at the line of scrimmage . The loss leaves coach Jesse Minter's team on the verge of falling out of playoff contention in the much more competitive AFC North, where all three division foes have a 6-4 record or better. The Panthers started the season relying on the strength of Bryce Young 's arm, but it was Chuba Hubbard who helped deliver the knockout blow against the Saints. The Canadian-born running back ran for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught five passes for 80 yards as Carolina overcame 17 penalties for 152 yards to snap a three-game losing streak. “We didn’t play the perfect game,” Hubbard said of the Panthers, the NFL's most-penalized team . “Obviously, we won and it feels good, but there’s a lot of things we got to clean up. ... At at the end of the day, a win is a win.” Wins have recently eluded the Ravens, who've struggled to find consistent quarterback play since the injury to Lamar Jackson . Baltimore traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett and the passing game made strides against the Chargers. But the running game, which has long been Baltimore's bread and butter, can't seem to get on track. Derrick Henry has failed to eclipse 60 yards rushing in his past five games, and was limited to 10 yards on 10 carries by the Chargers, although he did score twice. Minter called the team's struggles in the run game “unacceptable.” “There’s to me just a combination of a lot of factors that we need to figure out how to be able to run the football,” Minter said. “There’s been spurts of it, but the last few games, it’s obviously not where it needs to be. It starts with me, starts with the coaches, goes down to the players." The Panthers have been one of the league's worst run defenses this season, but have shown signs of improvement the past two weeks under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash. Carolina held the Denver Broncos and Saints to a combined 131 yards on 50 carries, a 2.62-yard average per carry. Need to know Baltimore (4-6) at Carolina (4-5). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m., EST, FOX. Latest odds: Panthers by 2 1/2. Against the spread: Ravens 2-8, Panthers 4-5. Last week: Ravens lost to Chargers 23-20; Panthers beat Saints 20-17. Last meeting: Ravens beat the Panthers 13-3 on Nov. 20, 2022 in Baltimore. Series record: Panthers lead 4-3. Matchup to watch Ravens WR Zay Flowers vs. Panthers CB Mike Jackson . Flowers is sure to be plenty motivated after a costly late fourth-quarter fumble against the Chargers prevented the Ravens from having a chance to tie the game and send it into overtime. Jackson returns from a six-game absence with a groin injury, giving the Panthers some much-needed experience in the secondary. He led the NFL in pass breakups last season with 19. Stats and stuff — Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was deactivated this week and will not play Sunday after derogatory comments he made about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. Humphrey had said the city was “best at making criminals.” — The Ravens have failed to score more than 20 points in their past five games. — Brissett finished 33 of 49 for 340 yards against the Chargers with no touchdowns and one interception. — TE Mark Andrews had a season-high 82 yards receiving on eight catches against the Chargers with Brissett at the helm. — If the Ravens lose, it will be their longest losing streak since the end of the 2021 season. — Hubbard needs 42 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown on Sunday to match Christian McCaffrey as the only players in franchise history with 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of the season. — The Panthers are expecting three players back from injuries this week. — The Panthers are 4-1 all time in overtime games under head coach Dave Canales . — WR Jalen Coker failed to catch a pass last week against the Saints and has just seven catches on 18 targets for 74 yards and one touchdown reception over the past four games. That's a huge drop-off in production from the first four games when he was targeted 35 times and caught 24 passes for 319 yards and two touchdowns. — Panthers OLB Jaelan Phillips earned NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors after having five tackles, one sack, two quarterback hurries, and a fumble recovery against the Saints. — Carolina is 22-13 in one-score games since Canales took over in 2024. ------ AP Sports Writer Noah Trister in Baltimore contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Hard-luck Rams catch break in Puka Nacua suspension
stories.summary: It figures that in a season this sideways, the best break the Rams have caught in weeks came from the people who just suspended their best player. Somewhere in the...
stories.detailText: It figures that in a season this sideways, the best break the Rams have caught in weeks came from the people who just suspended their best player. Somewhere in the NFL offices, somebody signed off on a three-game suspension for Puka Nacua. Somewhere in Los Angeles, somebody had to look at the calendar and think, well, if you insist. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua reacts after winning an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders in Landover, Md., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Nacua can serve all three games while he’s on injured reserve. The shoulder pads were going to stay in his locker anyway. When he’s healthy enough to put them back on, his suspension will already be behind him. How often this season have the Rams been able to say something worked out about as well as they could have hoped? Certainly nobody was saying it after the Denver game. The Rams had a game they should have won, the kind you circle when you’re trying to figure out how a team with this much talent ended up having to fight this hard just to keep its head above water. Just look at who has been hit by injuries. Myles Garrett. Nacua. Davante Adams. Cornerbacks Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie. That’s a whole lot of the blueprint spending time on the injury report. The Rams built this team to pressure quarterbacks, cover receivers and make defenses account for two dangerous targets. Injuries have reached into every one of those plans. Sean McVay has spent too much of this season figuring out what’s left to work with each week. They’ve also had more experience than anybody around here wanted finding out what the offense looks like with one of its best players standing next to McVay. There’s a reason a coach spends all week drawing up ways to get the ball to somebody. The guy behind him might know exactly where to line up. There’s still the matter of what happens once the ball gets there. With Nacua, sometimes the best part of the play starts right about where it should end. A defender gets his arms around him a yard short of the sticks, and somehow it’s first down. Try finding that on the call sheet. That still leaves the Packers, the Chiefs and the 49ers on the schedule without Nacua. Go ahead and read those names back to McVay and see how lucky he feels. Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders in Landover, Maryland, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Getty Images Except the Rams were going to play those games without him anyway. And that’s where the calendar did them a favor. They’ve already been figuring out how to win without Nacua. Now they just have to do it a little longer. Maybe the catches come from three different guys against Green Bay. Maybe the running backs have to carry them against Kansas City. By the time San Francisco rolls around, nobody will care if the same formula worked twice. Now imagine getting word that Nacua is healthy again and having to explain to the rest of the locker room that it’ll be another three Sundays before anybody gets to see him play. That was the danger. The timing of the suspension took it off the table. Which brings us to Apollo 13. At some point on that flight, everybody involved had to let go of whatever they thought the mission was going to look like. They had duct tape. They had some awfully smart people on the ground. They had a bunch of stuff on board originally intended for other purposes. What could they piece together that would get three astronauts back to Earth? For the Rams, Earth is the playoffs. Get there however you can. Win an ugly one. Ask a backup to give you one good afternoon. Give the defense a lead late and let somebody on that side close out the kind of game that got away against Denver. Then come back Monday and see who can practice. For all that’s gone sideways, the Rams are still alive. And the team an opponent draws in January could look a whole lot more like the one we expected in September than the one McVay is trying to hold together in November. Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates a fourth-quarter touchdown with Head Coach Sean McVay in Landover, Maryland, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Getty Images Nobody asks how much duct tape it took once you land. And if the Rams get there with Nacua healthy, good luck to the defensive coordinator who spent the last month watching film of an offense that had to make do without him. All the Rams need is a way in. From there, they have a chance to run the table. Funny to think, after everything that’s happened to them, who just helped keep the door open.

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football . Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. stories.title: Bears' Jeffery Simmons says knee injury a non-issue, expects to play vs. Saints
stories.summary: Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said the knee injury that held him to limited participation in practice this week wouldn't keep him from playing Sunday against the Saints.
stories.detailText: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons dispelled concerns about his availability for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints after a knee injury held him to limited participation in practice. "Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he said, referencing his No. 99 jersey and a popular T-shirt that Bears fans created when he was traded to Chicago. "I'll be out there Sunday." Simmons' remarks came after he missed Tuesday's practice and showed up on the team's injury report as a limited participant on Wednesday (an estimation) and Thursday. He sported a brace on his left knee when he returned to the field Thursday. "Things happen in this league. It's kind of like when I put the elbow brace on, there was a lot of questions," Simmons said, referring to his 2024 ulnar collateral ligament injury with the Titans. "But I feel fine, practiced today. Practice went great. I've been seeing a lot of things on Twitter about the '99 problems.' That won't be a problem this Sunday." Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said he does not believe Simmons' knee injury will impact his availability against the Saints. "I don't anticipate any issues with him," Allen said. The Bears sent their 2027 and 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-rounder to Tennessee on Oct. 29 in exchange for the All-Pro defensive tackle. Chicago also received a 2028 fifth-round pick. Simmons had an immediate impact on the Bears' defense upon his arrival. He logged 87% of defensive snaps in his debut at Seattle, where he tallied six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a defended pass in Chicago's 34-17 win. He followed that performance with another four tackles (one TFL), one sack and a defended pass in the Bears' Week 9 win against the Buccaneers when he played 97% of defensive snaps. The Bears have allowed 4.5 yards per play with Simmons on the field (in 110 snaps) compared with 11.4 yards per play when he's not in the game (10 snaps). In two games, Simmons has faced a double-team on a team-high 24 pass rushes. "With him commanding that much attention, it opens up some one-on-one opportunities for some other guys and I think some other guys have benefited from that," Allen said. "I think that's a positive thing that we have. I think the more really good players you have that have the ability to win their matchup -- whether that's a matchup in coverage, a matchup in the run game, a matchup in the passing game -- winning these one-on-one matchups are big in our league. "Obviously when we can get him in a one-on-one, it's a great thing for us and a lot of times the offense is going to give a lot of attention to him, and so some other guys are going to have to step up." Bears general manager Ryan Poles described Simmons' addition as "a shot in the arm" for a defense that was forced to work around injury constraints along the defensive line to generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Since Simmons' arrival in Week 8, the Bears' defense has recorded a blitz rate 20 percentage points lower across 69 dropbacks with the defensive tackle on the field, blitzing on 21.7% of those plays compared with 41.7% of the 230 dropbacks with him off the field, according to Next Gen Stats. Simmons' off-field impact has been felt as strongly as his contributions in games. When asked Thursday whether the Bears' defense needed a leader like Simmons after seeing the response since his arrival, Allen agreed. "Well, maybe to that extent, yeah," Allen said. "And yet, look, we've always had a group of guys that come in and work and do the things that they're being asked to do to perform at a certain level. I think he just accentuates that." If Simmons records a sack against the Saints, he will tie the longest streak of his career at three games. Coming off a Week 10 bye, Chicago is expecting the return of running back Kyle Monangai , who missed five games with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai has been a full participant in practice along with wide receiver Luther Burden III , who is out of the concussion protocol, and cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe). Nickel corner Kyler Gordon is the only player on the 53-man roster who has not practiced this week as he recovers from an injury to his left shoulder sustained in Week 9. Coach Ben Johnson classified Gordon's injury as "day-to-day."

stories.title: Saints, Justin Reid 'working through' potential release
stories.summary: Saints and safety Justin Reid are "working through some things" regarding the veteran safety's potential release, defensive coordinator Brandon Staley said Thursday.
stories.detailText: METAIRIE, La. -- The New Orleans Saints and safety Justin Reid are "working through some things" regarding the veteran safety's potential release, defensive coordinator Brandon Staley said Thursday. "I think that's going to come to a resolution here shortly," Staley said. Staley said Reid's request took him by surprise, and said Reid has mostly spoken with Kellen Moore about it this week. "Justin's been a professional since he's been here and I know that I've really enjoyed working with him. There's some things that we all want a little bit more of from a productivity standpoint. But in terms of the fit, in terms of how he's been here, he's been a pleasure to coach. So we'll just leave it at that," Staley said. Reid, 29, had been with the Saints for two seasons after signing a 3-year deal worth $10.5 million annually during the 2025 free agency period. Reid had one year remaining on the contract, which he restructured in March to lower his cap number to $5.2 million. He is the second team captain to ask for his release in a year after wideout Brandin Cooks asked for and was granted his release a year ago. It took several days after Cooks was granted a release by the team to become official as both sides worked out a resolution. "I think the football business side of things is different than the culture of the locker room," Staley said. "I think just speaking for our defensive culture, it's been strong for two years. I think that we have a very close group. I think that this group of guys has really come together the right way. I think last year, losing Demario [Davis], there were a lot of questions on what our defense would look like. And I think that we've been able to answer that so far with the production of our group and then also the connection of our group. "I think that that's been a strength of ours and we continue to play the right way, practice the right way. I think this is just one of those things ... it's just a football business matter and these things happen. And again, I'll leave those specifics to Kellen." Reid was voted a team captain in both of his seasons in New Orleans, but struggled this season with the Saints secondary giving up an average of 231 yards per game (21st in the NFL). Reid publicly argued with fans on X after the Saints gave up more than 400 yards in a 45-24 primetime loss to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 4. Reid pushed back against a fan that said he didn't make any plays. He followed up with a now-deleted post the next day saying "I'm a grown man FROM Louisiana. I don't need coddling from nobody but some of yall trying to make it seem like I don't care or show low effort. On the contrary I probably care the most!! I probably should not of got on twitter so quickly after the game but I'm upset too. I got pride and I ain't just gonna be punching bag for negativity and be silent about it." "Justin has been a professional since he's been here. I know I've really enjoyed working with him," Staley said. Reid was selected by the Houston Texans in the third round of the 2018 NFL draft. He also spent three seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs , where he was a part of two Super Bowl winning teams. "We never know what people are going through," safety Jordan Howden said. "So like I said, it's the next man up and we all got a job to do. Somebody has to go out there and play. We got to step up and be ready for this weekend. So he's my brother and I hope everything's good, but we still got a job to do." New Orleans.Football first reported the news that Reid had requested his release.
