stories.title: Could Gennings Dunker’s return revive the Steelers’ jumbo package?
stories.summary: The rookie third-rounder may not start, but he could still help keep the Pittsburgh run game rolling.
stories.detailText: Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images | Getty Images Despite being a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Iowa tackle-turned-guard Gennings Dunker seemed destined for a redshirt rookie season with the Steelers. Dunker was buried on the depth chart over the summer, missing some time with injury and then opening the regular season as a gameday inactive. Then, in late September, he landed on injured reserve with a reported MCL sprain. Pittsburgh opened Dunker’s 21-day return window from IR on Wednesday, the same day the team placed starting left guard Mason McCormick, who is expected to sit out until the playoffs, on the injured list. And although the Steelers’ coaching staff has said the usual platitudes regarding Dunker’s development so far this season, the rookie’s lack of experience thus far makes it clear that backup lineman Spencer Anderson will be the new starting left guard for the immediate future. Of course, there’s a chance Anderson underperforms or Dunker impresses enough over the next few weeks for the rookie to overtake the veteran in the starting lineup. But whether or not that does happen, Dunker could still play a notable role for the Steelers as the sixth lineman in the offense’s jumbo package. The Steelers started using their jumbo package this season in Week 7, a 16-10 win over the Saints where Pittsburgh rushed for 148 yards. It appeared again in Week 8’s victory over the Cleveland Browns, where the Steelers managed 200 yards on the ground. Anderson, of course, has served as that sixth lineman in the jumbo package for the Steelers in recent seasons, with Pittsburgh making the package part of its offensive identity in 2025 under then-coordinator Arthur Smith. New head coach Mike McCarthy made the choice to emphasize it once again midway through 2026, and the results were still overwhelmingly positive. According to Sumer Sports, Pittsburgh averages +0.25 EPA per rush when using its jumbo package in 11 personnel this season, well above the team’s still-good +0.06 EPA per rush across all personnel. Per a detailed breakdown from BTSC’s Ryan Parish following the Browns game, the Steelers earned a first down or touchdown on 37.5% of their runs out of a six-lineman package in Weeks 7-8. Why did McCarthy take so long to come back to the jumbo package? A number of reasons could be in play, including game-by-game matchups and Pittsburgh’s rash of wide receiver injuries in recent weeks. However, McCarthy also hinted after the Saints game that the team didn’t use the package early as Anderson began the season in the starting lineup before suffering a reported bone chip injury in late September. Once Brock Hoffman took over as a starting guard and Anderson was healthy again, the latter was available to play as the sixth lineman and the jumbo package suddenly reappeared. With Anderson about to go back into the starting lineup, it might not be a great sign for the future of the jumbo package. But Dunker might be able to fill that role. The Steelers seem to like Anderson as the sixth lineman because his athleticism (9.35 RAS as a guard) and versatility make him a strong candidate for the almost pseudo-tight end nature position. Dowdle 9 yd TD run McCormick/Fraizer double & climb + Hoffman/Iheanachor double & climb + Fautanu & Washington on islands to set the edges + Anderson in motion to lead block through C gap. Hoffman loses his guy so Rico makes him miss, then takes the knifing in CB for a ride pic.twitter.com/cYmCvI4cHW — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 The Steelers didn’t seem to like Hoffman in that role while Anderson was the starter as the former scored just a 4.19 RAS at guard and has largely been an interior player over his career. Those same concerns shouldn’t apply as much to Dunker, who has a 9.61 RAS as a guard after playing tackle during his Iowa days. And while Dunker is still learning as a pass blocker, his road-grading ability in the run game should translate to the pros more immediately. Every Gennings Dunker run block rep vs. the Bills in preseason Week 3: Man, Dunker is an absolute bully. #Steelers pic.twitter.com/869EufoaxQ — Tommy Jaggi (@TommyJaggi) August 28, 2026 Beyond that, Dunker’s mean demeanor in the ground game fits perfectly with the bully-ball identity of the Steelers’ jumbo package. Despite Pittsburgh moving Anderson back into the starting lineup following McCormick’s injury, the pending activation of Dunker might not spell the end to one of the Steelers’ most successful offensive packages this season. And facing a bottom-10 rushing defense in the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, Sunday’s game could be a good place to start.

stories.title: Washington Commanders unveil 'Beer Spear' ahead of 'Hail Raiser' debut on 'MNF'
stories.summary: The limited-edition collectible vessel can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it.
stories.detailText: Monday marks the Washington Commanders ' debut of their new alternate uniforms, the "Hail Raiser." The Commanders will be ringing in the all-black threads with a similarly themed concession item: the "Beer Spear." It's a limited-edition collectible vessel that can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it. Featured on the vessel is the Commanders' new W-spear logo, which also appears on the Hail Raiser helmet. The logo includes a gold spear interwoven into a burgundy "W" with gold outline. The Commanders announced the new item Thursday. It will be available for purchase at select concession stands during the rest of the Commanders' home games, starting on "Monday Night Football" against the Cincinnati Bengals . Washington already boasts a crab stuffed pretzel at its concession stands. The pretzel is shaped like a crab and is filled with lemon tarragon crab dip topped with garlic butter and grated parmesan cheese. The beer spear is just another in the list of creative sport-related concession items that deal with beer. Some MLB teams have the "beer bat." The NHL's Buffalo Sabres introduced the "beer sabres" last season, while the Philadelphia Flyers countered with the "beer skate." Each of them became instantly popular among fans and collectors alike. Teams haven't stopped experimenting for similar items, and with a beer spear now off the table, the natural evolution could be a beer shield.

stories.title: Sam Hartman's next drive: 'The Bachelor' questions answered
stories.summary: A guide to the Commanders quarterback's upcoming search for love and how his NFL commitments could shape the season.
stories.detailText: At the Washington Commanders ' Thursday practice, a dozen or so cameras trained on the club's fourth quarterback. Normally, this player would be ignored during a shooting period, but Washington's fourth quarterback is Sam Hartman , who despite having never played in an NFL regular-season game, will be the next lead of "The Bachelor" in the 30th season of the show. After a good throw, Hartman said to the other three quarterbacks: "I hope they post that one." At the end of the throwing session, a Commanders player said to the media focused on Hartman, "Do you guys want a hair flip?" When Hartman, the practice squad quarterback known for his movie-star quality hair, was announced as the next Bachelor last week, he became the second active NFL player to take the lead title. His short and sweet "Good Morning America" appearance left both football and "The Bachelor" fans with many pressing questions and hilarious hypotheticals. What happens if the 3-5-1 Commanders miraculously make the postseason and they need Hartman but he has to go film "The Bachelor"? With the show premiering on March 21, just 10 weeks after Week 18 and nine weeks after the wild-card round, will Hartman have to leave for the Bachelor mansion in California to begin filming? Though Hartman hasn't played in a regular-season game, he has served as the emergency third quarterback for a stretch in each of the past two seasons, and with the state of the Commanders' often-injured quarterbacks room, does this production schedule mean the backup to the backup position could end up in jeopardy? (this might seem farfetched but the Commanders played their third-in-line quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis in London this season, when starter Jayden Daniels was out and then backup Marcus Mariota got hurt). And "The Bachelor" franchise has historically had a no phones policy for participants. While Hartman will not be demanding a huge crowd of clubs in free agency, how will he stay updated of any new offers if he finishes the season on the practice squad and becomes a street free agent? Will he have his phone to talk to his agent? Fear not, for Hartman addressed the media Thursday after practice and ESPN has attempted to answer these extremely urgent questions for the sake of Commanders fans and contestants vying for his attention, who might be curious about his NFL obligations and financial status going forward. Let's start with the basics. How did he become a candidate for "The Bachelor"? Hartman told reporters Thursday that ABC reached out to him, "just kind of out of the blue." He said Wake Forest is a "pipeline" for "The Bachelor." Hartman is the third Wake Forest football alumni to participate in "The Bachelor" franchise. Matt James and Tyler Cameron also played for Wake Forest. The ACC Network called Wake Forest "Bachelor U" on Instagram after Hartman's announcement. Has an active NFL player done this before, and what distinguishes Hartman's situation from previous athletes in the franchise? The current host of "The Bachelor" franchise, Jesse Palmer, was the first professional athlete to appear on the show. His season aired in April 2004 when he was the Giants ' backup quarterback. Palmer, a fourth-round draft pick, started in three NFL games during his career. Former NFL tight end and "The Bachelor" contestant Clay Harbor (100 games played, 39 starts) recently vented on Chicago station 104.3 The Score about Hartman's lack of NFL playing experience. "You present yourself as an NFL player and you have never taken an NFL snap in an NFL football game," Harbor said. "I take a little bit of an exception, that's a little bit of false advertisement." What should viewers know about his college and NFL career? Not much to see here in terms of NFL action. Hartman went undrafted and has never played in a regular-season game, but he has seven preseason appearances. In college, Hartman played five seasons at Wake Forest and transferred to Notre Dame for his final year of eligibility in 2023. He led Notre Dame to a 9-3 season where they outscored opponents 509-207 . What is his current roster status? Hartman is currently on the Commanders' practice squad, which means he attends meetings and participates in practice like every player on the active roster, but he does not dress on game days and he cannot play in a game unless he is elevated to the active roster. Hartman has been elevated to the active roster twice in his three seasons with the Commanders and has served as the club's emergency third quarterback for the first five games of his rookie season in 2024 and the last two games of the 2025 season, when Daniels and Mariota were injured. As the emergency third quarterback, Hartman was a game-day inactive and did not count toward the 53 active players on game day. How much money does he make? Hartman's practice squad contract pays him $247,500 for this season if he remains on the practice squad for the rest of the season. If he is elevated to the active roster, he would earn more money. As an undrafted free agent in 2024, the Commanders reportedly paid Hartman one of the biggest guarantees of all undrafted free agents: a $20,000 signing bonus and $225,000 base salary guarantee. What will happen to him after the NFL season? When Hartman's practice squad contract expires (one week after the final game of the season) he becomes a street free agent. This means he will be immediately available to sign with any other club and does not have to wait for the new league year to begin on March 11, like an unrestricted free agent. The Commanders have the option to sign him to a futures contract to hold his rights, like they did in 2024 when he also finished the season on the practice squad. In this scenario, phone access could be important because he might have offers from other NFL clubs to consider. If he is elevated onto the 53-man roster this season (a real possibility since he has been in each of his past two seasons), then he will become an exclusive rights free agent, meaning the Commanders have the first right to "tender" him to a new contract, and if they choose to do that, he will not be able to negotiate with any other club. Has Hartman ever seen an episode of the show? No. He told reporters he is open to advice, and to please let him know any dos and don'ts. "I'm gonna probably do some tape watching after the season's over, and study up, get the DVSport clicker going kind of break down, go from first down to second down, third down, and finally end at the fantasy suites." How will he balance football and filming? When does filming begin? There is no set schedule for filming yet, but Hartman told reporters, "Once the season's over, I'll head out." ESPN also confirmed with ABC that "The Bachelor" will start filming after the Commanders' season ends. So, breathe easy, Commanders fan, your quarterback depth is safe, all the way down to QB4. Hartman's NFL agent Brian McLaughlin told ESPN that the "Filming schedule is still being worked out to accommodate the [Commanders'] schedule. He did run it by the team and they understood." ABC declined to comment what locations Hartman would be traveling to, but historically the show begins filming in L.A. and then travels -- both domestic and international -- as the season progresses. How long is production expected to last? Unknown. The production timeline varies from season to season. "The Bachelor" is filmed in advance, rather than airing live, so Hartman's time in front of the cameras will be wrapped before it premieres. Does filming overlap with team workouts, minicamp, training camp? No. After the Commanders' season ends, Hartman has no further obligations to the team until April, which is the start of voluntary offseason training activities. Before being cast, did he discuss participating with his team and did he need permission? Hartman said Thursday that he talked to "everybody that needed to be talked to, and they were very supportive, and that was much appreciated by me." McLaughlin told ESPN that Hartman "ran it by the team and they understood." He declined to provide further details. Will he have access to his phone or communication with his team and agent during filming? ABC declined to comment on whether Hartman will have access to his phone during production. But phone access for leads is not unprecedented. In an interview on the "Call Her Daddy" podcast, the most recent Bachelorette Taylor Frankie Paul said she negotiated phone access during production to keep in contact with her three children and to promote the reality show that made her famous, "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives." McLaughlin declined to comment on Hartman's phone access. He joked: "I plan on standing outside the mansion and yelling offers to him over the gate. I'll call the mansion landline worst-case scenario." Does Hartman's participation involve any restrictions related to NFL or team branding? An NFL spokesperson replied to an email with this question and said: "No." All right then! Brand freedom! Get ready for a lot of cringe-worthy Commanders puns. Hartman is already testing out some football-themed one-liners. In his scrum with reporters Thursday in the Commanders' locker room, he said he's looking for "his future teammate for life." When will the contestants be announced? There isn't a set date for the contestant announcement, but typically it is published a month ahead of the premiere date. What has Hartman said about why he wants to participate and what he's looking for? On "Good Morning America," Hartman said that when he was first presented with the opportunity to be the Bachelor, "I was like, no way... I just think there is the connotation of it and I was like I don't know... " But then he said he talked to Palmer about it, and that changed his mind. "He gave me the insight, what is it and what it's not," Hartman said. "If you get told, hey you get a chance to go find the love of your life, I know one thing, when people are saying I do, they don't ask you where you met, they just ask if you want to do it forever." Hartman said Thursday that he believes he can find love on a reality show and he's there for the right reason. "That's definitely the huge objective of it all," he said. "To go on there with any other reason wouldn't be fair to the TV show or the girls." He said his Commanders teammates were giving him advice after they found out the news and his parents told him to be himself and to "trust your instincts and trust your gut." "I'm very nervous," Hartman told GMA. "I have a tough time having a conversation with one girl, 30 is going to be pretty tough." As for what he's looking for in a match, Hartman said, competitiveness. "I think somebody that I want to be able to chase, not chase in a way like you haven't texted me back in a week but chase in a way that they have a drive for something and it motivates me to want to wake up and chase them," he told GMA. "I think we have some really cool stuff planned and they have to be ready to bring their competitive spirit." He said his family works in medicine, his dad as an orthopedic spine surgeon, his mom as a labor and delivery nurse, and his brother as a medical resident at Vanderbilt, so he's looking for a partner who is also interested in caregiving. Will football be part of the dates, and could former/current teammates or coaches appear? Hartman told reporters Thursday that his teammates knew he was the Bachelor two weeks before the announcement. As far as their potential involvement in any episodes of the show, Hartman said, "I'd bring the whole team if I could." Despite never watching an episode of "The Bachelor," he said he knows about the hometown visits that happen toward the end of the season. "Kind of a meet the family thing, maybe I'll just bring the whole team because that is my family right now," he said. "They probably know me the best in the world, so I think that would be a good barometer for her and myself to see what I'm about and what she's about." "The Bachelor" Season 30 premieres Sunday, March 21 (8:00 p.m. ET), on ABC and streams next day on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S. ESPN Washington Commanders reporter John Keim contributed to this story.

stories.title: Brock Purdy’s embarrassing viral moment resurfaces with Vikings twist
stories.summary: Brock Purdy this week was reminded of an embarrassing viral moment from the last time he and the San Francisco 49ers played in Mexico City.
stories.detailText: Brock Purdy has become one of the NFL’s most efficient quarterbacks thanks to his ability to execute. But that doesn’t mean he hasn’t had a misstep or two with the 49ers. San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One notable miscue resurfaced this week ahead of Purdy’s return trip to Mexico City , where he last played during garbage time of a blowout win over the Cardinals in 2022 when he was Jimmy Garoppolo’s backup. The 49ers were leading by 28 points with just over seven minutes remaining, and Purdy was sent in to relieve Garoppolo and salt the game away. On one play, Purdy took a shotgun snap and turned left to hand off the ball to running back Jordan Mason, who went to the right and forced Purdy to keep the ball. The play was botched, but Purdy wound up scrambling for a 6-yard gain while “Monday Night Football” broadcasters Joe Buck and Troy Aikman poked fun at the rookie who was the last pick in the NFL draft. Buck noted the 49ers called Purdy, at the time, “Baby Bosa” because of his thick legs. Aikman, laughing, added, “Baby Bosa needs to know which way to turn to hand off.” The play came up this week because Purdy was asked about it by reporters on Thursday ahead of San Francisco’s trip to play the Vikings at Azteca Stadium . Oddly enough, the running back in the play, Mason, will be on the other sideline Sunday night after the 49ers traded him to the Vikings in March 2025 for fifth- and sixth-round draft picks. Jordan Mason #27 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball against the Green Bay Packers in the fourth quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday, September 13, 2026, in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Getty Images “It’s funny now,” Purdy said Thursday. “In the moment when I’m a rookie, I’m trying to prove myself to Kyle [Shanahan] and my teammates. So I was stressing over it after that. But it’s funny that I got an opportunity after that, and we went and had success.” That game was Purdy’s third career NFL appearance. He didn’t throw a pass as the 49ers ran the ball to kill the clock in the 38-10 win. But history changed two weeks after that gaffe when Garoppolo injured his foot against the Dolphins, forcing Purdy to become the team’s starting quarterback. He completed 25 of 37 for 210 yards with a touchdown and interception in relief helping the 49ers win, 33-17. Purdy went on to win his next five starts and two playoff games against the Seahawks and Cowboys before suffering a torn UCL in his throwing elbow early in the NFC Championship game against the Eagles. The 49ers lost that game but made it to the Super Bowl the next season with Purdy under center, and he hasn’t been called “Baby Bosa” since.

stories.title: Cardinals’ Carson Beck pops up on injury report in latest QB setback
stories.summary: Cardinals fans may be holding their breath going into the weekend over whether Carson Beck will be able to play on Sunday against the Chiefs.
stories.detailText: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) warms up before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams in Glendale, Ariz., Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Cardinals fans may be holding their breath going into the weekend over whether Carson Beck will be able to play on Sunday against the Chiefs. Beck was placed on the Cardinals’ injury report on Thursday as a limited participant due to a back issue, raising concerns about whether he will be available for the Week 11 game, which would reignite the quarterback shuffle that Arizona has gone through this season. The rookie quarterback had been dealing with back spasms a few weeks ago, according to Cardinals reporter Dani Surreck . Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) warms up before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams in Glendale, Ariz., Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images Arizona Republic Cardinals reporter Theo Mackie noted in a post on X that Beck had been in the team locker room after practice and “seemed to be walking around normally.” An update on Beck’s status will take place on Friday when the team releases its final injury report of the week. While Beck’s stat line didn’t appear to be anything special, reviews of his first NFL start — a 34-6 loss to the Rams — were more complimentary. He finished completing 11 of 18 pass attempts for 108 yards and had two interceptions. “I think the overall operation of our offense was really good,” Beck told reporters after his first game. “That’s something that [head] coach [Mike] LaFleur talks about a lot is the operation [and] getting in and out of the huddle. There were a couple communication things that [for] the first time being out there — calling plays again in a live game and live action and just getting better, being more clear and concise with the huddle, being able to get in and out quickly and get on the ball and snap it right. “Everything that you can control before the ball is actually snapped and there are live bullets flying, but I think that was good. Just going where the defense told me to go, reading the defense, reading out our plays and trying to give guys opportunities to make plays. For me as a quarterback, that’s what I’m here to do. Run the offense, have great operation, get in and out of the huddle and then ultimately play clean football. I think that’s something that this offense can do.” If Beck isn’t able to go on Sunday, Josh Johnson and Joey Aguilar are the Cardinals’ backup options.

stories.title: Packers Roster: Green Bay’s emergency signing board
stories.summary: Here is who the Packers have worked out this year and how/when they can become available to the team
stories.detailText: (Steve Russell/Toronto Star via Getty Images) | Toronto Star via Getty Images Throughout the season, the Green Bay Packers bring in players for tryouts to either push the current practice squad as an immediate signing or to build a board of emergency players if a few injuries start to build up in the future. Since it’s the bye week, I decided to take a fresh look at all of the players that the Packers have brought in so far in 2026 (56 in total) and paint a picture of who is still available. We’ll break these tryout players down into five groups: Players who are signed with the Packers Players who are signed with other NFL teams Players who are available to sign Players whose rights have been claimed by UFL teams Players who are coming off a CFL season Players who are signed with the Packers QB Cam Miller – PS WR Coleman Owen – PS, previously 53 WR Quincy Skinner Jr., PS TE Kenny Fletcher Jr., PS OL Kevin Zeitler, 53 OL Mekhi Becton, PS to 53 DL Haggai Ndubuisi – international exemption, PS DL Mazi Smith, PS ED D.J. Johnson, PS LB Jack Dingle, PS CB Elijah Culp, PS S John Saunders Jr., PS The Packers have signed two offensive linemen to their 53-man roster after tryouts (Kevin Zeitler and Mekhi Becton), but Becton was initially signed to the practice squad before being promoted up. Currently, 10 of Green Bay’s 17 practice squad spots have been filled by players brought in on tryouts. The only practice squad players who have been with the team since training camp are WR Isaiah Neyor, TE Drake Dabney, OL Dalton Cooper, OL Dillon Wade, ED Arron Mosby, ED Nyjalik Kelly and CB Domani Jackson. Players who are signed with other NFL teams RB Damon Bankston (Vikings PS) – previously on Packers PS RB Phil Mafah (Giants PS) WR Bryce Oliver (Texans PS) WR Dontae Fleming (Giants PS) OL Cordell Volson (Seahawks PS) – previously on Packers PS DL Gabe Hall (Eagles PS) LB Josh Ross (Vikings PS) S Juanyeh Thomas (Cowboys PS) None of these players are available for the Packers to sign to the practice squad, since they are already signed to another team’s practice squad, but Green Bay could sign them to the 53-man roster as a poach. If the Packers sign another team’s practice squad player, they must guarantee that player’s pay and roster spot for three full weeks of the regular season. Players who are available to sign QB Carter Bradley RB Ian Wheeler TE Cody Hardy TE D.J. Rogers TE Zack Kuntz OL Robert Jones DL David Blay Jr. – previously on Packers PS DL Eric Johnson II – previously on Packers PS DL Isaiah Iton DL Jalen Hunt DL Zxavian Harris ED Cruz Smith – international exemption eligible ED Dasan McCullough ED Seth Coleman LB Cam Riley LB Channing Tindall LB Curtis Jacobs LB Deion Jones LB Reid Williford CB Ambry Thomas CB Cobee Bryant S Kahlef Hailassie – previously on Packers PS S Sanoussi Kane S Wande Owens P James Rendell These are players who are completely on the street. If you want to think about the emergency board, these are the bones of that board right now. Players whose rights have been claimed by UFL teams QB Jack Plummer (Storm) – retained QB Jalen Morton (Aviators) – retained WR Nick Nash (Storm) – draft TE Zach Davidson (Kings) – retained ED Vincent Anthony (Aviators) – draft LB Chris Paul (Renegades) – draft CB Dwight McGlothern (Breakers) – draft CB Miles Battle (Defenders) – draft S Chris Edmonds (Battlehawks) – draft P Jack Stonehouse (Renegades) – draft The UFL just had its draft, which included teams selecting multiple Packers visitors to the league. Players with the “retained” label are 2026 UFL players whom Green Bay worked out, while players with the “draft” label are new players to the UFL whom the Packers worked out before they were picked in the recent draft. Players who were picked in the recent draft are not all under contract with the league yet, so there’s no guarantee they even play spring ball. Usually, the UFL allows its players to seek NFL employment up to the week after the Super Bowl. If players sign reserve/futures contracts with NFL teams, though, they become ineligible to play in the upcoming UFL season, as they’re under contract with another league. Players who are coming off a CFL season CB Zy Alexander (Stampeders) This one is a special case. The Packers worked out cornerback Zy Alexander, coming off a season in the CFL, last week. Alexander cannot sign with an NFL team (would likely be a reserve/futures deal) until after the regular season is over, but he also cannot sign with an NFL team after the CFL free agency period starts in early February. So right now, Alexander can’t sign with an NFL club, but he will have a window when he can be added. He can currently work out with teams, though, as long as NFL clubs file a request with the player’s CFL club (which can’t be denied).

stories.title: Five reasons why 'Madden' movie fails miserably | Opinion
stories.summary: Nate Davis watched "Madden" - now streaming on Prime Video - so you don't have to. Here's why the movie fails miserably.
stories.detailText: "You gotta be authentic." It's a line uttered by actor Nicolas Cage as he portrays the eponymous protagonist in "Madden." Unfortunately, he's central to a movie that fails to live up to that credo and doesn't seem to have much Commitment to Excellence in its bid to depict Pro Football Hall of Famer John Madden . The movie, which began streaming on Prime Video on Wednesday, Nov. 18, opens with a black title card, which says, "Not all of this happened ... but most of it is true." That effectively sets a tone for a movie that lacks drama, and − yep, authenticity. And while that might merely describes this movie's issues in broad brush strokes, "Madden" really flops for these five reasons: 1. Nicolas Cage While you might not think the 62-year-old Oscar winner would be a natural choice to play Madden, Cage put on 25 pounds and supplemented his weight gain with another 30 or so pounds of prosthetics to achieve something of a physical resemblance to the portly coach of the Oakland Raiders , TV analyst and entrepreneur. Yet Cage's creative direction is baffling. He commits to his version of Madden's voice, but he sounds nothing like the man − to the point of distraction. But that's hardly the most jarring aspect of his performance. Regardless of whatever phase of his career he was in, Madden was always an outsized character. And while he might have bordered on cartoonish as a coach, pitchman or, certainly at times, in the broadcast booth, he was nothing if not genuine and inimitable − plus brilliant in his various capacities. But Cage gives a rendition that's more a buffoonish caricature of an inattentive family man who dreams up football schemes with his head in a refrigerator (don't we all). Anyone who draws a first impression of Madden, imperfections and all, from this movie isn't likely to form an image of the man described by his players, colleagues, friends and family through the decades. A disservice to his memory? You decide. 2. Boring football scenes David O. Russell directed "Madden," though NFL Films was involved with the project − and football aficionados will certainly recognize some vintage football sequences intercut into the film. Otherwise? If you're not a football fan, "Madden" isn't likely to make you one. The movie essentially starts with the 1976 AFC Championship Game , during which Madden's Raiders were poised to finally vanquish their archnemeses, the Pittsburgh Steelers , after years of falling short to the 1970s' preeminent dynasty. But in a failed bid to interject some sense of drama, the Steelers score first in "Madden," even though they never actually led in a game Oakland won 24-7 in reality. And while there's some acknowledgement of the tension that existed at the time between these franchises, "Madden" doesn't attempt to illustrate the backstory of Oakland's failures against the Steelers, including the "Immaculate Reception," Pittsburgh coach Chuck Noll suggesting there was a "criminal element" to the Raiders, nor is there much exploration of the colorful characters on both teams. You might also come away thinking all football games are played inside stadiums with high concrete walls covered in bunting. Snippets of Cage using a telestrator? As silly as you might imagine. And scenes of actors playing football aren't value-added in the least − no reason to try and improve on NFL Films' capture of Hall of Famer Willie Brown's 75-yard pick-six in the Raiders' Super Bowl 11 blowout of the Minnesota Vikings , Madden's crowning achievement as a coach ... not that the point is driven home all that well in the movie. 3. Wasted cameos Snoop Dogg and former NFL stars Marshawn Lynch and Julian Edelman appear in "Madden." None do much more than serve as set pieces, Snoop the only one to even get a few lines − those serving to convey the cultural phenomenon that is EA Sports' "Madden NFL," which Madden himself was instrumental in developing, marketing and legitimizing. Seems like a squandered opportunity given the outsized personalities of this trio ... and, if I'm being honest, I didn't even realize Edelman was in the movie at all until I scanned the closing credits. WORST SPORTS MOVIES: Will 'Madden' join their ranks? 4. The movie should have been called 'Davis' Leave it to Batman to steal the show. But Christian Bale's depiction of Raiders owner Al Davis really stands out in this flick. Bale managed to replicate Davis' distinctive look, through various times in his life, as well as his signature Brooklyn accent. His relationship with his wife, Carol (played by Sienna Miller), comes across as far richer and more nuanced than Madden and his wife, Virginia − though Kathryn Hahn does a nice job in the role. But watching Bale as the recalcitrant, paranoid, renegade boss of the Raiders − and Madden's lifelong friend, despite the strain football often put on their relationship − leaves the viewer wanting for more, especially since Davis' football legacy is equally impactful to Madden's if not as well known or understood in pop culture. 5. 'Madden' isn't fun but is boring You'd think a movie about a larger-than-life persona like Madden's would be entertaining, at least largely so. Not the case here. "Madden" literally put me to sleep for 20 minutes even though its run time comes in shy of two hours. You'd think it would lend itself to humor. But that winds up being quite forced − whether it's Cage puking while battling an ulcer, Shane Gillis' fictional character Vince McGary as Madden's neighbor, or Cage and Bale listening to N.W.A. on the Madden Cruiser ... which hardly seems to serve a purpose and certainly doesn't much illustrate the Raiders' ethos, especially when they were based in Los Angeles at the time the hip-hop super group rose to prominence. Want a gripping, accurate feel for John Madden? I'd point you to Fox's documentary "All Madden.," which premiered on Christmas Day 2021, just days before Madden's death . Thankfully, that's the one the man himself got to see . All the NFL news on and off the field. Sign up for USA TODAY's 4th and Monday newsletter . stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 8: Ja'quan McMillian #29 of the Denver Broncos reacts during the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The news breaking of the $67M contract extension for cornerback Riley Moss was well-received by most fans. As it should, he’s been the primary focus of targets with Pat Surtain II opposite him and he has held up as well as any number one guy on any defense. He probably could have gotten close to $20M a year and Denver got him for $16.75. A very good deal. That said, it would still be a mistake for the Denver Broncos to let fellow cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian walk in free agency. McMillian is just a playmaker and you cannot put a price tag on that or find any easy replacement. They will have same issue if/when Marvin Mims Jr. walks, although he has been a bit quiet this year so far on the playmaker side of things. We asked fans a month ago who they felt the Broncos should keep if they only kept one and the vote was quite literally one-sided: The funny part about that is even those of us who voted McMillian would also love to see Riley Moss around too. He has been a very good outside cornerback, but McMillian has made the big plays in key moments. Those monster plays stick with you when you think about who has made a bigger impact. Hopefully Denver finds a way to keep both and gets McMillian locked down long-term ahead of free agency next year . Broncos daily recap Broncos vs. Raiders: 3 Things to Watch in Week 11 The Denver Broncos host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely in their Week 11 matchup. How the Denver Broncos can beat the Las Vegas Raiders In order for the Denver Broncos to defeat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, here are three things they need to accomplish. Broncos looking to start second half of season on a high note The Denver Broncos are back to business this week and will host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Despite a 4-6 record, Head Coach Sean Payton knows they’ll be a tough team to beat. Potent quotables Sean Payton On if he can tell what the bye week did for the team physically “It’s hard to tell. I think you never can control obviously your bye. I’m sure there are a handful of players that may not have been able to play had we have played last Sunday that will have a chance of playing this Sunday. I thought we had good work. It was a good full practice longer than two weeks ago. Yes, it went well.” On if he knows Raiders Head Coach Klint Kubiak “I know his father [former Broncos Head Coach Gary Kubiak]. I know he was here. [He’s] one of the guys I spent a lot of time with. I have a ton of respect for their family and what he’s doing. There are a lot of ties just to that organization. I think already you can see it on tape what they’re wanting to build and the early success this year. You go through Kansas City, Seattle, Buffalo, these are all teams that are in the thick of it, and they played all those teams to one-score games.” On if the Raiders’ offense has changed with a new starting quarterback “There’s a system they believe in though, and you still saw it in the game they played last week. So they’re going to do a good job with the run game, the play-action off of it. Fortunately we’ve had a week at least to see tape on the new quarterback. You have to defend the offense and then obviously the people in it.” On what he likes about what the team is doing right now “It’s a little bit more than halfway in the season, and there’s a lot that still needs to be done. I feel the same way about our team. We knew going in there was a challenge to the start of the season based on the opponents. You get so micro-focused on just the next game and the things that these guys do well. They return kicks well. They punt it well. They force fumbles better than anyone in the league. They’re really good offensively, red zone. They’ll possess the ball if you allow them to. They do a really good job of the time of possession. The takeaways have been noticeable. I don’t know if that answers your question, but rarely do you really take a bigger picture look. You’re aware of where your team’s at, but then you’re also very mindful of the things that we need to continue to improve on.” On how the offensive line can block better “There are times in a game where there are going to be some looks that are tougher looks. There were some opportunities against Carolina where we could have been a little bit better, a little cleaner.” On how taking the whole bye week off benefits the team and his conversations with Chiefs Head Coach Andy Reid about it “Remember it wasn’t like we split the atom when he gave me that answer. It’s a long season. I think guys get away mentally, and physically, the guys that were or currently are injured are here. It’s good to have everyone back.” On Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza’s first start last week “It’s a tough start obviously when you play the Super Bowl champion. I remember his college tape well. All of us that would go through the draft process. Obviously he’s a winner. The things I see really are just from afar, but you see the quick release and all the things you’re looking for in that position. I’ve heard nothing but great things from people that have been around him.” On if the evaluation of quarterbacks in the draft process is the same when there’s not need at that position “It is. We’re not going to have a private workout, so maybe to some degree it isn’t also. Fair question. I just remember what it was the year [QB] Bo [Nix] came out. The tape evaluation, the grades, the reading of the player, that’s very much the same, the time you spent. You don’t really try to hurry through position groups. You really try to put grades and discuss players, and you have plenty of time to do that.” On if the notion that rookie quarterbacks struggle in their first few starts is overblown “There have been great debuts. You could go back and find an argument probably for a lot of [players], and a lot of it may be circumstantial relative to the surrounding cast. This clearly is a different team than we’ve played the last couple of years. That’s the part where you see [Head Coach] Klint [Kubiak]’s imprint, the people that are there coaching from top down.” On TE Caleb Lohner returning to practice “It’s good to get him out here. He’s worked his tail off. Today was his first practice. He was making a lot of strides, and that setback was unfortunate, but he has that spirit, that will. You never felt like he lost interest. So it was good to see him moving around.” On if WR Courtland Sutton’s ability to win a release in the short red zone has improved since he arrived “It’s a strength of his. He’s real good at the line. His size, he uses his hands well. I think it’s something that for him, being in the paint, if you will, as a power player is something that he excels at.” On if he looks for the ability to release when grading receivers before the draft “I think you’re looking for stop start, you’re looking for transition. I like bigger receivers in our league period. That doesn’t mean entirely, but the target radius and all those things are quarterback friendly with him.” On if Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson’s injury during a celebration is a teaching moment “I’m kind of with [Lions Head Coach] Dan [Campbell]. I saw the final comments. We’re teachers and we’re constantly… But we’re going to walk out of the doors, and there’ve been a lot of celebrations. I’m kind of with Dan there where it’s unfortunate. Two good players got hurt on the same play, and I think that there are a lot of other things that I would put on tape on a Friday, Saturday that are [teaching moments]. That, I wouldn’t put that on.” On if he takes pride in watching a former player and coach like Lions Head Coach Dan Campbell handle adversity “Yes, absolutely. He was that way… I was a young assistant with the Giants when we drafted him out of [Texas] A&M. I was with him in New York his first four years. Then I go to Dallas. I kind of speak on his behalf, we sign him there. We’re together there. We counted the years once. There was a clip where he was somewhere else, then at Miami and then back coaching. He’s always been gritty, tough, dependable, reliable—all the traits that you admire as a player, you see now as a coach, as a communicator. Very quickly I think that team has kind of taken on his personality, and it’s been a real good fit for that city. He’s real authentic.” On if he watched football on Sunday “Yes, I watched Sunday. I watched the Seattle game, and then the ones prior, not maybe as much.” On if he can scout while watching on TV “The TV copy gives you a different perspective. You hear the audio relative to injuries, and you’re watching. It’s different. When you put the all-22 on, you’re like, ‘OK. I didn’t get that with this play, but I see it now.’ So it’s a different watch. Nonetheless, I think it’s beneficial.” On if he ever watches the TV copy when reviewing film “Believe it or not, in our cut-ups, you can set this setting—mine is set right now—to go wide copy, end-zone copy, end-zone copy, TV copy. So if I want to see the TV copy or hear the audio of something, I can. I usually click through it, but sometimes if there’s something that I… If I see an opposing quarterback maybe look like he audibled now that we put microphones everywhere, we have to change them… So I’ll go to the TV copy to see if I heard was he changing a play or not, that kind of thing.” On if he pays attention to the TV analysts while watching “Not really. I know that there are a lot of games televised. The only big difference for me is years and years in the NFC, there was more FOX. Then here, much more CBS. I would say that’s the noticeable difference.” On if he saw anything while reviewing film that he wants QB Bo Nix to improve on “I think the one thing that’s changed… Fair question. The old bye week was the collection of… We get such updated information, it’s now do you want now’s information the week you’re not playing because you had it last… In other words, it’s much more available, quicker each week. There’ll be a self-scout we pay attention to. I like how he’s playing, progressing. We keep looking at that.” Bo Nix On being on the ManningCast this week and the reaction from his teammates “It was fun. They (Pro Football Hall of Fame QB Peyton Manning and former Giants QB Eli Manning) do a really good job. Obviously, I’ve known those guys for a while. They always have great attitudes and are great guys to talk to. They are extremely funny and they have great personalities. At the same time, they are the Mannings, so they have great football minds, too. It’s fun to get on and talk with those guys. It was a great environment and easy conversation. It was all good.” On how he feels about the offense trending in the right direction “I think even if we were playing great that we would feel really good. I think with the numbers and stats, we will always want more. That’s the thing about stats is that they are never good enough. For us, it’s always about the win column and being efficient and helping our team by playing complimentary football. Overall during the season, we’ve done that. When we’ve needed to score, we’ve scored. When we’ve needed a stop, we get a stop and then our special teams are playing really well. Overall as a team, we are playing well and complimentary off of each other. We just need to finish strong. We haven’t really done much yet, so we have to keep going.” On if there is an added sense of urgency coming off the bye week entering the second part of the year “You’re refreshed and you get going, so you have a second wind. I think there is something to that. The first part of the season is really tough coming out of the gate after training camp, so you get to the bye and that is always a point to regroup and go from there. I think we’ve put ourselves in a spot to now make the push and really get going. There is an element to the peak of the season. We’re almost to that point and almost to the end in December and January, where the games get really important. Not that they weren’t already, but those have playoff implications and then you run into the playoffs. You want to be confident going into those. Right now is the stretch as a team that we can’t let off and really continue to press.” On if he believes the offense has gotten into a groove the last few weeks “We have to keep progressing and everyone on the team will tell you that there is room for growth. I’m not too worried about the things that come with the wins. It’s all about, ‘Did I put my team in a spot to win the game?’” On his connection with WR Courtland Sutton “No. 1, he does a great job of using his physicality down in the red zone. He’s a big body, so that helps. When the field gets tighter, he is able to go up for the jump balls and he is able to create space. Then at the end of the day when the game is on the line and it’s red zone time, he just knows that is his area and where he is strongest at… When I get to him and he’s open, that’s always the best part of the play. I know he’s going to come down with the catch in the end.” On if his mentality of peaking at the right moment helps him get through the season “Absolutely. In the NFL, there are so many weeks that you have to put your head down and just keep working. One week could look completely different and one week doesn’t tell the story for the next week. For me, it’s a marathon and not a sprint. You can’t wear yourself out early. You don’t want to peak too soon. It’s just sort of the game within the game of the season. It’s finding ways to get better so that when that moment comes and the playoffs are here and when you have to win the football game, you’re not going home early because you missed out on your peak. Coming off the bye, we feel fresh, we feel good and ready for this next stretch.” Pat Surtain II On the environment at Empower Field at Mile High for opposing offenses and quarterbacks “We have a pretty tough environment for opposing quarterbacks. It’s never easy going on the road against our crowd and obviously against our defense. That’s going to be big-time this weekend, just affecting the quarterback and communicating will be hard as well. It’s always tough going against our crowd, which is an advantage for us.” On the challenge of playing against Raiders TE Brock Bowers “Some people think that he’s a tight end, I think he’s a receiver the way they utilize him in the route tree. I feel like his route tree and his yards per target is very telling. They utilize him in a multitude of ways that you have to be keyed in about. It’s all about honing in on the details and understanding how they’re trying to use him.” On what he sees from the Raiders offense this season under Head Coach Klint Kubiak “It’s a different offense, like more of that West Coast offensive feel. They want to get started on the run game, and that leads to the play-action and stuff like that. It opens up their offense even more. They utilize a whole lot of personnel, 13, 12, 11, whatever how you look at it. It’s going to be a test for us just to get lined up in matching personnel.” Courtland Sutton On what he sees from the Raiders this season “Someone asked me this weekend about divisional games. I tell you all the time, every game weighs as heavy if it’s the next one, but divisional games obviously carry a little bit more weight in the overall standings of things. The one thing that I’ve learned, noticed and have witnessed myself is it doesn’t matter what a team’s record is when you’re talking about divisional games because they’re going to show up and play hard no matter what. The Raiders have always been that team. No matter what their record is, they always show up and play the Broncos really hard. I wouldn’t expect them to do anything different. To answer your question, on film you can see. You watch the games, and they’re in a lot of these games against really good teams. Record may not show it, but that’s a really good team that plays really hard. Going back to [Raiders Head] Coach [Klint [Kubiak], they have a really good leader over there. I wouldn’t expect them to come in and do anything else than to give us their best.” On the wide receiver group’s mentality and how guys have stepped up “I think we got to see it at different parts of the season so far in different games, if a guy goes down here, if a guy goes down there. The thing that I appreciate and I love about our room is the next-man-up mentality. You never want to see your brother go down, but whenever someone does go down, we still have to go out there and perform. To see guys go out there and not only know what to do, but to go out there and perform at a high level… Some of the plays that [WR] Troy [Franklin] executed in the game, he didn’t even practice throughout the week. He just went out there, and he knew the job assignment, and he went out there and made plays. ‘Marv’ (WR Marvin Mims Jr.) as well. Some of the things that ‘Marv’ was doing were some of the plays that were for [WR] Jaylen [Waddle] and Jaylen got hurt. ‘Marv’ stepped up and knew what to do. Troy stepped up and knew what to do. [WR] Pat Bryant had a really good game. I think our room—and I say it all the time—our room is very deep. We have a lot of talent in our room. A lot of people may not know a lot of names in there, but their names will continue to get buzzed around the league because whenever it’s time for them to step up and go out there and perform, they do that. I appreciate that for our room because it allows us to be able to be more versatile.” On tying Ring of Fame WR Demaryius Thomas for the fifth-most starts at wide receiver in team history “It’s humbling. Anytime someone tells me my name getting buzzed around anything that he [Ring of Fame WR Demaryius Thomas] has done, it’s truly humbling and heartwarming because I know how much he means to this franchise, and organization and to this city. To be able to have that many games under my belt, which honestly shocked me. I had no clue before literally I came up here on the podium that it’s going to be 125 games. I was like, ‘Daggum.’ I didn’t know that. You go into each season, you want to be healthy. You want to do your best but then also you’re chasing a Super Bowl. You don’t think of how many games, this amount of games, that amount of games. It stacks up. It’s truly an honor. I’m truly humbled to be able to have that milestone be crossed and for it to be around the same time as my brother being here as well. I’m grateful. stories.title: Aidan Hutchinson shares thoughts on injury: ‘I always come back stronger’
stories.summary: Aidan Hutchinson speaks for the first time since tearing his ACL.
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Aidan Hutchinson #97 of the Detroit Lions looks on during the second half of an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on November 8, 2026 in (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Detroit Lions All-Pro defensive end Aidan Hutchinson took to social media to deliver a message to fans for the first time since tearing his ACL in Week 10 against the New England Patriots in Germany. Hutchinson’s injury occurred moments after a drive-ending sack of QB Drake Maye, as the star edge rusher leaped in celebration and his knee buckled on landing. The perennial Defensive Player of the Year candidate will require surgery, and his 2026 season is unfortunately over . Here’s the message Hutchinson wanted people to see: I honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won’t hold me back. I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him. Very grateful for all of your prayers and well wishes. Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger. 2. That’s the last time I go airborne 😁👍 Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys. Hutchinson is no stranger to recovering from season-ending injuries. In 2024, he broke his leg and spent several “miserable” days in a Dallas hospital, and gained a new perspective on life . Early signs for Hutchinson are that he didn’t suffer any other significant knee damage, but they can’t be certain until the surgery takes place. If it goes well, he’s expected to have a chance to recover and return to play sometime in 2027, hopefully “stronger,” as he did after his 2024 injury. View this post on Instagram

stories.detailText: Marred with injuries, it’s been a frustrating season for the Los Angeles Rams’ wide receiver corps thus far and already without its top two pass catchers — their situation nearly just got worse. Puka Nacua has been suspended three games without pay for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, the NFL announced on Thursday. In addition, the league reportedly communicated to the superstar wideout that any further violation “will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the League.” The NFL said it also communicated to Puka Nacua that that “any further violation of the Personal Conduct Policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the… — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 19, 2026 The move stems from an apparent incident on New Year’s Eve 2025, where a woman alleged he bit her on the shoulder and made an antisemitic remark. Although she filed a civil lawsuit against Nacua on March 25, his attorney denied any remarks were made and classified the alleged assault as “horseplay.” Despite currently being on injured reserve with MCL and PCL sprains as well as turf toe , the suspension will take effect immediately — making Nacua eligible to be reinstated ahead of Los Angeles’ Week 15 game against the Dallas Cowboys — one week before they’re set to visit the Seattle Seahawks. It currently remains unclear if he’ll be cleared to suit up when first eligible to return. However, considering the Rams placed him on injured reserve ahead of Week 10, he was already poised to miss a minimum of four weeks. In essence, Nacua won’t miss any time as a result of the suspension. As for the financial punishment, he was fined $961, 167 — a sixth of his 2026 base salary. There is precedent for players like Nacua getting suspended while on IR, although the other examples are not nearly as prominent in the NFL. Puka Nacua’s suspension was imposed when the process was complete. Discipline is not delayed when a player is on IR. Daniel Ekuale, Sam Williams, Mike Woods and David Parry are among those who served suspensions while on IR. https://t.co/oPSdmhNBUw — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 19, 2026 In his continued absence, Los Angles will seemingly continue to lean on a mix of veterans and far less experienced receivers — although WR Davante Adams (ruptured hamstring) could potentially return in the coming weeks and take on the lead role until Nacua is eligible to take the field. stories.title: NFL puts product over principles with Puka Nacua suspension | Opinion
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Rams' star wide receiver is taking a $950K hit for a 2025 biting incident, but won't miss time with a suspension overlapping his IR stint.
stories.detailText: The NFL is tarnishing its precious shield with its suspension* of Puka Nacua – even more than the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver did with his reprehensible behavior. The league has known since March that Nacua was being sued by a woman who said the player had bitten her on the shoulder during a New Year’s Eve dinner, where he also allegedly said something antisemitic. But it wasn’t until Thursday, Nov. 19, when Nacua is conveniently already on injured reserve, that the NFL saw fit to suspend him . Follow along while I do the math: NFL players on IR have to miss a minimum four games before they can return. Nacua, who missed the first of those four games last week while dealing with a knee injury , is now suspended for the next three weeks. Which means Nacua won't miss any more time than the Rams were already accounting for, and they – and the league – will get one of their biggest and most-productive stars back, healthy and rested, just in time for 6-4 Los Angeles to make a push for the playoffs. Unless you’re a Rams fan, that stinks to high heaven. No reason NFL had to issue Puka Nacua suspension now What Nacua did was apparently bad enough to merit a three-game suspension, but not bad enough for the NFL to shut him down when it would actually matter? So what, exactly, is the point of suspending Nacua at all? Because it sure doesn't tell him, or anyone else, that there are consequences for unacceptable behavior. (Nacua's suspension* will cost him close to $1 million in lost salary. That'll be pocket change when he signs a new contract in the offseason, to say nothing of the endorsement money he’s still getting.) Apparently, the story the NFL is spinning is that if Nacua messes up again, the NFL disciplinarians are really going to let him have it! They pinky swear it! Yes, the leagues' collective bargaining agreement with its players allows players to serve suspensions while on IR. That’s not the point. The point is everyone has known for almost nine months that Nacua was going to be suspended, and the NFL just so happened to choose the least-inconvenient time possible, for both Nacua and the Rams, to do it. A time that helps preserve Los Angeles' hopes for a Super Bowl 61 appearance at SoFi Stadium, its home arena. Other suspensions have been dragged out because of ongoing legal cases. That's not an issue, here, however. Nacua was never charged criminally. The civil lawsuit against him has not been resolved. If the NFL has already waited nine months to hand down punishment everyone was expecting, what difference would it have made for the league to wait another three weeks? Except for the impact it would have on the Rams' playoff chances, that is, and the all-important postseason intrigue for a major-market NFL team. Other players who served suspensions on IR not high-profile It is also true that other players have served suspensions while on IR. According to Adam Schefter , Daniel Ekuale was given five games for violating the performance-enhancing substances policy after suffering a season-ending injury last year. In 2024, Sam Williams was suspended three games for violating the personal conduct policy while out for the season with a torn ACL. Mike Woods got six games in 2023 for violating the personal conduct policy when he was already out with a torn Achilles. In 2018, David Parry was suspended for four games for violating both the personal conduct and PED policies when his season had already ended because of an ankle injury. What’s the difference between them and Nacua? Ekuale, a defensive lineman, spent seven years in the league, making 21 starts in 64 games and recording six sacks. Williams, a defensive end, has five starts in 58 games over four seasons. Woods, a receiver, had 12 catches in 15 games. Parry, a two-season starter at nose tackle in Indianapolis, played in four games his final two seasons. Nacua is a two-time Pro Bowler who last year led the league with 129 catches and also had 1,715 yards receiving and 10 touchdowns. He's started all but one game he's played in his first four seasons, including seven this year. Despite missing last week, Nacua is fourth in the NFL with 70 catches. Nacua shouldn't be punished more harshly because he's one of the NFL's top players. But neither should his star status earn him any favors. The NFL is insulting everyone's intelligence by claiming to take anything that reflects poorly on the league very, very seriously and then turning around and making sure Nacua's punishment won't cause anyone any real hardship. The NFL's justice system has always been arbitrary. Turns out, it's not very just, either. Follow USA TODAY Sports columnist Nancy Armour on social media @nrarmour. stories.title: Why didn't the Colts trade Jonathan Taylor? RB spared in Indy's fire sale
stories.summary: The Colts decided to keep Jonathan Taylor beyond the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Here's why they didn't deal him in their fire sale.
stories.detailText: The Indianapolis Colts were the NFL's biggest sellers ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. They offloaded numerous veteran players, including wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs , defensive lineman DeForest Buckner and long-time, stalwart left guard Quenton Nelson . But even despite their activity level, the Colts didn't trade their biggest chip. Running back Jonathan Taylor remained in Indianapolis even after being the subject of persistent trade rumors leading up to the deadline. Taylor has long been a star running back since being selected in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. Still, many thought the Colts might cash in and unload the 27-year-old in a blockbuster deal to continue to add to their coffers of draft assets ahead of what figures to be a challenging rebuild. So, why did the Colts decide to keep Taylor? Here's what to know about their decision as they move forward with the star running back in tow. Why didn't the Colts trade Jonathan Taylor? The Colts didn't trade Taylor because they view the 27-year-old running back as a part of their future. Colts coach Shane Steichen spoke glowingly of Taylor when asked what it mean to keep him in the fold during a media availability the day following the 2026 NFL trade deadline. "He means a ton. He's a hell of a football player. I'm excited that he's here," Steichen told reporters Nov. 11. "It's awesome for the organization to keep, you know one of the best running backs in the league in your franchise moving forward." Taylor has certainly thrived across his seven seasons to date with the Colts. He has twice led the NFL in total touchdowns during his career, earned an All-Pro first-team nod in 2021, and is pacing for his fourth season with at least 1,500 scrimmage yards in 2026. Taylor is also under contract through the 2028 NFL season, so the Colts won't have to worry about locking him down to another deal while he remains in the prime of his career. That may have been part of the reason the Colts were only willing to consider moving Taylor in a "blockbuster offer," per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . The Colts received packages including a second-round pick and more for Taylor, but he remains under team control and can continue to serve as Indianapolis' offensive engine as the team rebuilds. It's also worth noting that Steichen expressed no worries about the relationship between Taylor and the franchise even after the persistent trade rumors surrounding the star running back. "I can't speak for him, but I know that last week, he said he's proud to wear the horseshoe," Steichen said. "And so like I said, I'm excited that he's here. He's a great freaking football player." And Taylor reiterated in a media availability of his own that he was happy to remain in Indianapolis. "No," Taylor replied when asked whether he wanted to be traded before the deadline. "Just regular scheduled programing Tuesday. Like it's all water under the bridge now." Will Colts change Jonathan Taylor's workload? While Taylor remained with the Colts, the 27-year-old may not handle his usual workload down the stretch of the 2026 NFL season. The Colts are sitting at 3-7 entering Week 11 and are highly unlikely to make any sort of playoff push during the second half of the season. As a result, the Colts have seemingly started to limit Taylor's workload, as he has averaged 17.1 touches per game since Week 7 while playing no more than 69% of the offensive snaps in any game. By comparison, Taylor averaged 22.8 touches per game and never played fewer than 71% of the team's offensive snaps across the first six games of the season. Taylor's slight downtick in production has coincided with an uptick in production from rookie backup Seth McGowan . The seventh-rounder averaged just four touches per game across the first six games of the season but has seen that number balloon to nine per game in his last four outings. Against the Dolphins, Taylor saw 18 touches while McGowan had 12 and scored a touchdown. That 60-40 workload split could end up being closer to the norm moving forward as the Colts look to keep Taylor fresh and healthy during what looks like a lost season. Colts RB depth chart Below is a look at the Colts' running back depth chart, which remains headlined by Taylor even amid his recent downtick in touches per game. Jonathan Taylor Seth McGowan DJ Giddens Davon Booth (practice squad) Giddens, a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, has played sparingly this season, logging six carries for 43 yards. All of those touches game in Indianapolis' 42-7 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8. Meanwhile, Booth is an undrafted free agent who currently resides on the Colts' practice squad. He spent the offseason with the Cleveland Browns before joining Indianapolis' practice squad on Sept. 1. Jonathan Taylor contract details Taylor is playing the 2026 NFL season on the final year of a three-year, $42 million extension he inked with the Colts in 2023. After this season, the two-year, $44 million extension he signed with Indianapolis on Aug. 6, 2026, will officially kick in. Below are the full details of the latter agreement, which will keep Taylor under contract with the Colts through the 2028 season. All details are via Spotrac.com . Term : 2 years Total value : $44 million Average annual value (AAV) : $22 million Guaranteed money : $39 million Taylor's $22 million AAV ranks third league-wide among running backs. Only Jahmyr Gibbs ($22.5 million) and Bijan Robinson ($22.5 million) are making more. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Why didn't the Colts trade Jonathan Taylor? teamStories.detailText: DENVER -- — Top draft pick Fernando Mendoza 's first career road start comes against Denver's dominant defense , one week after he was sacked half a dozen times by the Seattle Seahawks in his NFL starting debut . “I believe getting thrown in the fire is the best way to learn, and the Seahawks and the Broncos both have considerably elite defenses,” the Las Vegas rookie said as he prepared to lead the Raiders (4-6) against the host Broncos (7-2), who have won five straight. Of course, Mendoza has high praise for everybody else, too. “I really believe every NFL defense is elite because when you’re playing at this level, the margin for error is so small, and all the defensive coordinators are geniuses,” Mendoza said in his aw-shucks kind of way. “So, I’m honored and blessed to go against a great defensive coordinator in coach Robbie (Rob Leonard) every single day, especially in OTAs and fall camp and training camp. So, I believe that’s helped prepare me, and now I’m excited to embark on this journey with my teammates.” Vance Joseph's defense has an NFL-best 157 sacks over the last 2 1/2 seasons, and the Broncos are coming off a bye week, so they're healthier with starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and Brandon Jones (hamstring) both returning to practice this week along with cornerbacks Riley Moss (concussion) and Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle). Broncos QB Bo Nix is making his 45th career start Sunday and he was asked this week to look back on his second career start, against Pittsburgh in 2024. “It's night and day,” Nix said. “My second start wasn't what I'm doing now. It's hard for a rookie quarterback. I don't care if you're sitting behind a guy like Kirk (Cousins) who you can learn from. You still have to go out there and ultimately play and ultimately do it. “And to his credit, he played a really good defense last week. He's going to play a really good one this week,” Nix added. “And it's just not easy and unfortunately the world's not going to give him any time to go through the obstacles that it takes as a rookie quarterback. But he'll continue to develop, he's a smart kid and he's played in big moments in college and I think that does translate.” The Raiders' 21-13 loss to Seattle last week marked Mendoza's first loss as a starter since Nov. 16, 2024, when he was playing for California and Syracuse defeated the Golden Bears 33-25. Mendoza went undefeated last season in leading Indiana to the national championship and capturing the Heisman Trophy. Need to know Las Vegas (4-6) at Denver (7-2). When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. EST, CBS. Latest odds: Broncos by 10. Against the spread: Las Vegas 6-4, Broncos 7-2. Last week: Raiders lost to Seahawks 21-13; Broncos had a bye. Last meeting: Broncos beat Raiders 24-17 on Dec. 7, 2025, in Las Vegas. Series record: Raiders lead 73-58-2. Matchup to watch Mendoza versus Denver's defense. The rookie has to deal with a unit that has racked up 26 sacks and has been especially disruptive with the return of Jonathon Cooper . Stats and stuff — Broncos coach Sean Payton can move into sole possession of 10th place on the career NFL victories list with a win Sunday. He's tied with Dan Reeves and Mike Tomlin with 201 wins, including the playoffs. — The Raiders are the 11th team to be 4-6 or worse after opening a season 3-0. Of the other 10 teams, only the 2009 New York Jets made the playoffs. — The Broncos have won an NFL-record 16 consecutive one-score games dating to last season. That's one more than the Peyton Manning-led Colts from 2008-09. — Mendoza became the fourth No. 1 draft pick at quarterback to have a rushing touchdown but no TD passes in his first start. Joe Burrow , Matthew Stafford and Steve Bartkowski were the others. — The Broncos are the only NFL team to start 7-2 in each of the last two seasons. — Maxx Crosby is the third player since 1999 with at least 70 sacks and 140 tackles for loss before his 30th birthday. Myles Garrett and J.J. Watt were the others. Crosby has been double-teamed or chipped 106 times, according to the NFL's Next Gen Stats, the most of any edge rusher. ------ AP Sports Writer Mark Anderson in Henderson, Nevada, contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
